539523|2026-06.headline: Alkem Q1 FY27 revenue rose close to 11% to INR3,740 crores, but net profit fell 21.7% on tax, and the Daman US plant received an OAI status.
539523|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR3,740 crores, up close to 11% YoY, with India at INR2,497 crores (+10.3%) and international at INR1,222 crores (+16%). EBITDA margin was 20.5% (EBITDA up 3.7% YoY), PBT was up about 1.8%, and net profit fell 21.7%, which management attributed to tax. Trade Generics was flat YoY in April-June, which dragged India growth, while branded generics grew about 12%. The Daman facility received an OAI status from the USFDA, which management says has not interrupted supplies.

financial_highlights.value: Improved QoQ and YoY, not quantified

segments.name: India formulations - Trade Generics
segments.commentary: Flat YoY in April-June after higher-single-digit growth in January-June; drag due to tighter receivables/DSO practices, API-linked price increases and competition. Management says it is number 1 or 2 in the segment.

segments.name: India formulations - Branded / non-trade (ex-Trade Generics)
segments.commentary: Branded generics grew about 12%; price up about 6%, new launches about 3%, volume about 2%. Chronic grew 17.9% vs IPM 15.4%; acute grew 12.3% vs IPM 10.1%.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Sales INR1,222 crores, +16% YoY. Management cites Chile, Australia and small high-growth markets such as Germany (35-40% growth) as drivers.

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: Management described US as challenging with little volume growth and near-flat price erosion; FY27 US guidance now high single digit to mid, helped by currency. Daman plant supplies about 45% of US revenue.

segments.name: MedTech (Occlutech and ortho)
segments.commentary: Occlutech acquisition completed mid-July, so no Q1 impact; ex-diligence, Q1 EBITDA loss of about INR5-7 crores from ortho/MedTech. FY27 target about INR400 crores sales for the roughly 8.5 months of ownership with breakeven EBITDA.

segments.name: US CDMO (Enzene, mAbs)
segments.commentary: Operating cost about INR60 crores per quarter; breakeven needs about USD25-30 million annualised revenue, now expected in FY28, with capex needed later and no US FDA approval yet on the facility.

guidance_outlook: US revenue growth now guided at high single digit to mid for FY27, versus earlier high single digit, with currency support.
India growth for the full year about 1 percentage point better than the prior guidance, which management put at close to 12%.
Gross margin guidance of 66.5%-67% maintained for the balance of FY27, with API price increases expected to weigh in later quarters.
Consolidated tax rate guided at 30%-32% (standalone earlier 27%-28%), because loss-making entities such as US Enzene carry no deferred tax asset.
Occlutech FY27 target about INR400 crores sales with breakeven EBITDA; EBITDA margin improving 7-8% YoY and reaching guidance over 3-4 years.
US CDMO expected to break even in 4-5 quarters per CFO, but MD later said it will not break even within 12 months; Trade Generics growth expected to recover to late single digits.
Denosumab biosimilar US approval delayed by at least a few months; Xgeva biosimilar EU launch about 3 months away; Tolvaptan US generic launch expected this quarter.
capex_capacity: Daman US facility received OAI status; corrective and preventive actions initiated, resolution expected in 6-12 months; 45% of US revenue comes from Daman.

Enzene US CDMO (mAbs, development to clinical supplies) operational since November 2025; capacity described as small but technologically differentiated; not yet US FDA approved; capex will be needed later, not this year.
Added about 1,200 MRs over the last few quarters, adding to employee cost.
Backward integration into 7 biosimilars in India generating about INR150 crores annual sales, with improved margins.
Acquisition of Occlutech completed mid-July 2026; integration started, with more India-operations integration expected from next quarter.
demand_pricing: India Trade Generics competition has intensified as large players entered; company also tightened receivable days, slowing primary sales.
Price in India ex-Trade Generics up about 6% YoY; US price erosion close to flat, which management says may have bottomed out.
Semaglutide going off patent is driving chronic market growth; Alkem's benefit so far is very small.
Gross margin improved on lower Trade Generics mix, stronger prescription business and currency; API price increases will weigh on later quarters.
Outperformed IPM in 7 focus therapies: anti-infectives 1.1x, gastro 1.2x, vitamins and minerals 1.4x, pain 1.8x, antidiabetic 1.4x, respiratory 1.6x, derma 1.6x.
Five US ANDA approvals in the quarter, one of them tentative.

qa_highlights.question: Why is India growth (10.3%) below most peers, and will it ease?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the drag to Trade Generics, which was flat to mildly up; branded generics grew about 12%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the cost increase is from CDMO and MedTech, and what are the losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost rose more than 16% from increments, about 1,200 added MRs and Enzene CDMO becoming operational in November 2025; US CDMO opex is about INR60 crores per quarter; ex-Occlutech MedTech losses are about INR5-7 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Trade Generics outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was flat in April-June after higher-single-digit growth in January-June; management expects recovery, and personally would be happy with late single digits over the next 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Occlutech outlook and margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target of about INR400 crores sales with breakeven EBITDA for about 8.5 months; the earlier 10% margin guidance is pushed out, reaching guidance over 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: How much of US revenue depends on the Daman plant, and are supplies affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Daman accounts for about 45% of US revenue; management says supplies continue without interruption and the impact is not expected this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate and US outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated tax rate is 30-32% because loss-making entities carry no deferred tax asset; US growth guided at high single digit to mid, helped by currency and not volume.

539524|2026-03.headline: Dr. Lal PathLabs Q4 FY26 revenue rose 16.6% to Rs 703 crore; FY27 guided to early-to-mid-teens growth and 27-28% margins.
539524|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 16.6% YoY to Rs 703 crore, driven by sample volume growth of 12.9%, while Q4 EBITDA rose 10.5% to Rs 187 crore at a 26.6% margin. Q4 PAT fell to Rs 132 crore from Rs 156 crore, as last year included a Rs 41 crore one-time benefit and this year had a Rs 30 crore Labour Code charge in Q3. FY26 revenue grew 12.2% to Rs 2,763 crore with a 27.2% EBITDA margin, and the Board approved a final dividend of Rs 4 per share. Management guided FY27 revenue growth to early-to-mid-teens and margins to 27-28%, while stepping up spending on labs, infrastructure and A&P.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 154 crore in Q4 FY25
vs Rs 156 crore in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Swasthfit (preventive B2C brand)
segments.commentary: Contributed 27% of FY26 total revenue; management says B2C is about 75% of revenue and packages make up about 28% of revenue, including Suburban packages.

segments.name: Delhi NCR
segments.commentary: Sustained double-digit growth through the year, with added testing locations to improve turnaround time.

segments.name: West / Suburban
segments.commentary: Suburban had weak performance for about 3 quarters but showed recovery in Q4; it is now reported within West and is no longer a separate entity.

segments.name: Radiology (Sovaaka and centres)
segments.commentary: One Sovaaka premium centre launched in January 2026; no further Sovaaka centres planned in FY27. One or two radiology centres are in the FY27 capex plan.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at early-to-mid-teens; CEO later framed it as a 13%-15% range.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 27%-28%, similar to FY26's 27.2% including the Rs 30 crore Labour Code charge.
FY27 capex guided at Rs 100-120 crore, covering maintenance capex plus 12-15 new labs, radiology centres and a precision lab.
Effective tax rate expected to stay around 25%.
Price increase not planned immediately; a decision is a few quarters away, depending on market response and competition.
International expansion: a Dubai/UAE subsidiary incorporated; over 3-5 years, new geographies including the Middle East are planned on top of Nepal and Bangladesh.
capex_capacity: FY26: added 14 new labs and more than 1,100 collection centres; about 32 labs and close to 2,000 collection centres added over two years.
FY27 plan: 12-15 new labs, 1-2 radiology centres and a precision diagnostic lab, on top of maintenance capex within Rs 100-120 crore.
Acquired Shahbazkers Diagnostic Centre, a single pathology-led lab in Mumbai with about Rs 6 crore revenue, for about Rs 20 crore (about 3.3x FY26 revenue); the EBITDA margin was not disclosed.
Sovaaka: one centre launched January 2026; management wants to stabilise it before any expansion.
Radiology expansion is to be slow and calibrated, with no ambitious 4-5 year targets set.
demand_pricing: FY26 patient volume growth was 5.3% (vs 4.2% in FY25); Q4 patient volume growth was 8.2%; sample volume growth was 12.9% in Q4 and 10.4% in FY26.
Tests per patient rose to 3.21 in Q4 from 3.07; revenue per patient growth was attributed to test and geographic mix.
About 39% of revenue now comes from Tier 3-plus towns; management says pricing is set by cluster, so Tier 3 growth is not dilutive.
Price increase deferred: last price rise was 3 years ago, but management is waiting because it passed on GST-related benefits.
Management said GLP-1 drugs had no differential impact on volumes.
Reagent supply: about 3-4 months of inventory and long-term contracts; a prolonged Middle East conflict could affect imported reagent supply and cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why is other expense up sharply in Q4, and is the margin sustainable into FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited infra upgrades including Delhi NCR and higher A&P spend as geographies expand; FY27 margin guided at 27-28% with investment in labs continuing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise about 19% YoY in Q4, and was there a regrouping?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 129 crore vs Rs 108 crore: courier and transport costs were regrouped from employee benefit to other expenses; the rise reflects 14 new labs and Sovaaka operations, not the Labour Code.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 tax rate near 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: A reversal of deferred tax after an income tax assessment and refund; the underlying tax rate is still about 25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the basis for early-to-mid-teens FY27 growth when the post-COVID run rate was 10-12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Lab and collection network additions are maturing, Delhi NCR is expected to keep growing at double digits, and Suburban is recovering; the range is 13-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Is GLP-1 adding to patient volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth reflects the collection and lab network and that no differential impact from GLP-1 is being ascribed.

qa_highlights.question: Is Suburban's revenue or margin separately reported, and where does its margin stand?
qa_highlights.answer: Suburban is no longer reported separately and is part of West; management said West margins still have room to improve, and the company-wide margin is 27-28%.

risks_watch: Q4 PAT declined 15% YoY to Rs 132 crore despite revenue growth, partly due to the absence of the Rs 41 crore one-time benefit from last year.
Margin pressure from heavy investment in labs, infrastructure and A&P; FY27 margin guided at 27-28%, which is flat to FY26.
Reagent and consumable supply and cost risk from the Middle East conflict after about 3-4 months of inventory.
Patient volume growth of 8.2% in Q4 may not be sustainable; management cautioned against building it into FY27 plans.
Price increase timing is uncertain; competitive intensity and market response will determine it.
Suburban recovery and West margin improvement are not separately disclosed, which limits tracking.

key_quotes: We are entering FY27 with strong operational momentum, a strengthened digital infrastructure, and a clear pathway towards sustaining early to mid -teens revenue growth.
So the 8.2% patient volume growth that we have seen in this quarter is something which I would not hastily built into the plan for next year.

The cluster pricing remains the same and parallelly, even when I am going into the Tier 3, Tier 4 towns, with more access, we will be able to sell our health packages, preventive check-ups and all of those, which even on a revenue side per patient side is slightly higher revenue.

539524|2026-06.headline: Dr. Lal PathLabs Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19.1% to Rs 798 crore, with EBITDA margin of 31.0%, and guidance may move toward mid-teens growth.
539524|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 798 crore grew 19.1% YoY, described as the highest quarterly growth in four years, led by patient volume growth of 8.2% and sample volume growth of 10.7%. EBITDA rose 28.7% to Rs 247 crore (31.0% margin) and PAT rose 27.2% to Rs 170 crore. Management said the CGHS/ECHS price revision adds 2-3% to realisations, and it may be more towards mid-teens revenue growth than early teens. Management will not revise the 27-28% margin guidance until after Q2, and leans towards reinvesting any upside.

segments.name: Swasthfit (bundled wellness packages)
segments.commentary: Growing about 20% YoY, but its share of revenue is flat at about 27% because total revenue grew at a similar pace. Management expects this growth to be sustained.

segments.name: B2C vs B2B
segments.commentary: B2C is about 75% of the mix and B2B about 25%, which management considers a good balance and intends to keep.

segments.name: Genomics
segments.commentary: Contributes less than 5% of the portfolio and is not yet moving significantly; management does not disclose it separately.

segments.name: West India (Suburban)
segments.commentary: Growth is close to double digits after LIMS integration. Suburban profitability is no longer tracked separately after its voluntary liquidation and back-end merger.

segments.name: Delhi NCR
segments.commentary: Management aims to grow it at double digits, in line with or close to overall revenue, and says it is achieving this.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth now seen towards mid-teens rather than early teens for FY27, versus the earlier guidance; the Q1 beat was slightly ahead of expectations.
EBITDA margin guidance of 27-28% is unchanged for now; management will reassess after Q2 and leans towards reinvesting any upside into growth.
Patient volume growth guidance of 6-7% for FY27 is unchanged; management said Q1 came in slightly ahead and that it is too early to call the full year.
CGHS/ECHS price uplift of about 2-3% at company level is expected to flow through for at least another 2-3 quarters and to support margins for one or two more quarters.
General price increase is not planned for H1; it will be reassessed towards the end of the year based on competitor pricing and cost pressures.
Capex of about Rs 140-150 crore per year; 12-15 lab additions planned for FY27 and 3-4 radiology centres (Delhi NCR plus 1-2 pilots in Tier 2 towns).
International business is a 3-5 year project; management has not set a contribution target and says it will remain below 5% for at least the next five years.
capex_capacity: Capex guidance of about Rs 140-150 crore for the year, covering maintenance capex plus high-end radiology centres in Delhi NCR and Tier 2 North India.
Plans to add 12-15 labs in FY27, similar to last year; network addition numbers are disclosed once a year.
Plans to add 3-4 radiology centres this year, mainly Delhi NCR plus 1-2 pilots in Tier 2 towns outside Delhi NCR.
Capacity utilisation is not disclosed; management says capacity is never a constraint in pathology.
Sovaaka premium wellness centre: only the first centre is launched and is in the learning and stabilisation phase; no scale-up yet.
demand_pricing: Patient volume growth of 8.2% was spread across geographies; management said it is too early to call a sustained shift from the 5.5-6% levels of two quarters ago, because the fever season has not yet started.
CGHS/ECHS price revision is worth about 2-3% of realisations; the rest of the 10% rise in revenue per patient came from test and geography mix, per management.
Industry growth acceleration is described as structural and broad-based across geographies, with no single trigger identified yet.
Competitive intensity is seen as staying high; management sees no structural price change in recent quarters.
Gross margin is near 81%. Management says higher-realisation tests carry higher COGS, so margin is unlikely to improve significantly.
Weather in Q1 was unusual (more heat, some showers), and its effect on diagnostics volume is not yet known.
Tier 3 and below is about 39% of FY26 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the realisation growth comes from CGHS/ECHS, and will it continue for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: CGHS/ECHS price increase adds about 2-3% at company level and should continue for at least another 2-3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will the guidance be upgraded from 27-28% margin and mid-teens growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is more likely to be mid-teens than early teens; margin guidance will be reviewed after Q2, with a lean towards reinvestment.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Swasthfit growth sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Swasthfit grew about 20% in Q1 and management expects this rate to be sustained, with traction in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Neuome and international plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Neuome (30% stake, up to Rs 3.5 crore) is a diagnostic supply-chain innovation play with operational benefit, not a new business. International is a long-term project: Ghana (80% of Sunshine Healthcare, up to GHS 45.6 million) and a Dubai subsidiary, with focus on Africa, Middle East, CIS and Southeast Asia; no target set.

qa_highlights.question: How should the cash of about Rs 1,700 crore be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Primarily M&A to build presence in the West and South, plus high-end radiology centres as capex on top of maintenance capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost as a percentage of revenue fall to 16.6%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this is a reclassification of logistics and courier costs out of manpower cost into other costs, applied like-to-like in the previous quarter too, not a structural change.

risks_watch: Margin guidance of 27-28% is not revised until after Q2; the CGHS/ECHS price pass-through is expected to support margins for only one or two more quarters, so the margin trajectory in H2 depends on reinvestment choices.

Patient volume growth (8.2% in Q1) is unproven as a sustained shift; management wants Q2 and Q3 through the fever season before drawing conclusions, and Q1 weather was unusual with effects not yet known.
General price increase is not planned for H1 and will be reassessed toward year-end based on competitor pricing and cost pressures; competitive intensity is expected to stay high.
Gross margin near 81% is not expected to improve materially; management flagged possible currency and inflation pressure on imported testing material if geopolitical cost pressures continue.
Employee cost ratio of 16.6% partly reflects a reclassification of logistics and courier costs, which limits like-to-like comparison with historical 18-19% levels.

Capital deployment of about Rs 1,700 crore cash is mainly directed to M&A in West and South India, with no deal size or timeline disclosed; international contribution is expected to stay below 5% for at least five years.
key_quotes: The CGHS, ECHS price increase is now flowing through into the system. Our assessment is that it kind of is to the tune of between 2%-3% at an overall company level.
So the idea always is to reinvest for future growth. That is the dominant idea.
I think we need the cycle to run through quarters for us to say that it has really caught on because we have not yet entered fever season this time round.
I do not think any of us are banking on competitive intensity reducing in this industry.

Management was also reticent on disclosures, declining to split genomics, Suburban profitability, and capacity utilisation.

539551|2026-03.headline: Narayana Q4 FY26: India margin rose to 25.1% (from 21.5%), but consolidated EBITDA dipped to ~20% on UK acquisition costs; management gives no formal guidance.
539551|2026-03.overview: Management highlighted high-end case mix and robotic cardiac volumes (about 100 robotic cardiac cases a month in Bangalore) driving India ARPP and margin gains. The UK business (PPG, acquired with five months in FY26) diluted consolidated margins and PAT; management says ~200 bps of the ~500 bps margin drop was one-time deal costs, normalising to ~22%. Cayman insurance losses (USD 5 million in the quarter) remain high, with a loss ratio of about 110–112% and price increases from June. India clinics continue to lose cash because of corporate overheads, and FY26 greenfield capex was only INR 109 crore against INR 424 crore planned.

segments.name: India hospitals
segments.commentary: Margin 25.1% vs 21.5% a year ago, attributed to transformation initiatives, robotic cardiac and high-end transplant work, and higher-configuration beds; volumes stagnated while ARPP grew. Mumbai (SRCC) broke even in Q4.

segments.name: India clinics and insurance
segments.commentary: Clinic and insurance losses flat at ~INR 66 crore in FY26; management expects similar cash burn into FY27 as 11 Bangalore clinics expand and Kolkata is added, and clinics will be merged into hospital reporting from FY27.

segments.name: UK (PPG)
segments.commentary: Five months consolidated in FY26; acquisition costs and transition/IT separation costs weighed on margin, and PAT is negative mainly from amortisation. Management says cash PAT covers the GBP 150 million 7-year loan, which is serviced in the UK.

segments.name: Cayman Islands (insurance and hospital)
segments.commentary: Insurance loss ratio around 110–112% (CIMA data); price increases on 30–35% of accounts in June; hospital revenue growth expected to slow from double digits as new client additions are slowed. Management asks analysts to view insurance and hospital together.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance; management declined to give ARPOB or top-line targets, saying rack-rate and price increases run at low-to-mid single digits.
Insurance losses expected to decline over about three quarters after June price increases; one or two more quarters of losses in the current range are possible.
Overheads expected to fall after UK integration; no date given for India insurance breakeven.
India capex of INR 3,000 crore across projects, with about INR 1,000 crore each expected to commission in FY28 and FY29; FY28 Rajarhat, HSR, Raipur and Bangalore timelines reaffirmed.
No additional capex planned for Cayman; UK capex plan to be shared later.
Mumbai expected to turn around once the adult programme starts; Bangalore clinics and Kolkata clinics planned in FY27.
capex_capacity: FY26 greenfield capex INR 109 crore against INR 424 crore planned; management blamed election-related labour shortages and permission delays.
Raipur: new tower to replace an old building; full capability set in place, no hospital-specific data shared.
Kolkata (RN Tagore) campus about 3.5 acres; Rajarhat project to add integrated quaternary capacity. Kolkata bone marrow transplant beds 10 versus 45 in Bangalore.
Management says construction costs are up about 60% over five years, and new hospitals are being built with more automation.
Clinic plan to double the current clinic count, with pace tied to property acquisition, rent negotiation and fit-outs.
demand_pricing: Bangalore: about 100 robotic cardiac cases a month and about 160 percutaneous aortic valve procedures in the cath lab; highest paediatric bone marrow transplant volumes.
North (NCR): management concedes it is very competitive; the cluster grew 7.5% in FY26 and Gurgaon/Dharamshila strategy is unchanged with no expansion plans.
Kolkata revenue share 26% growing only 5–6%; management expects volume growth in the next 2–3 quarters from digital marketing and clinics.
Patient volumes stagnated in FY26 while ARPP grew, as the mix shifted to advanced procedures and payer mix changed.
UK private-pay share was 7% at acquisition; management reports an absolute increase but gave no current figure.
Overheads rose ~8% against 10.2% revenue growth due to power and minimum wage inflation plus one-time merger costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Cayman insurance losses so high, and when do they reach breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Anesh Shetty said premium ramped faster than expected to ~USD 60 million annualised; losses should drop over about three quarters after June price increases and account pruning. Loss ratio is ~110–112% per CIMA data.

qa_highlights.question: Is UK EBITDA margin improvement sustainable and where did cost cuts come from?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandhya J said only two months of data existed at acquisition, and most savings are in overheads; IT separation is ongoing and a few more quarters are needed. Management expects overs and unders to neutralise.

qa_highlights.question: Why did India margins expand and is 25% stable?
qa_highlights.answer: Venkatesh cited transformation initiatives, high-end procedures, robotic cardiac volumes and higher-configuration beds; he said gains are sustainable but cited crude and dollar headwinds.

qa_highlights.question: Will the UK loan be serviced given weak PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandhya J said the GBP 150 million loan is serviced in the UK, the acquisition debt sits on the target's books, and cash PAT covers debt service; PAT is hit by amortisation of non-cash expenses.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Cayman hospital growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Anesh Shetty said double-digit quarterly top-line growth is not sustainable and new client additions are being slowed, while hospital margins were preserved.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 greenfield capex well below plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Viren Shetty said election-related labour shortages and permission delays caused the miss; FY28 commissioning goals remain.

risks_watch: Cayman insurance loss ratio ~110–112% and whether losses fall after June 2026 price increases and account purges.

India clinic cash burn rising with 11 Bangalore clinics expanding and Kolkata clinics in FY27.
Greenfield capex execution (INR 3,000 crore program, FY28–29 commissioning) after the FY26 miss.
Overhead inflation (power, minimum wages) and volume stagnation in India.
ROCE and ROE dilution during the expansion phase, per management.

539725|2026-09.headline: Gokul Agro Q2 FY27 revenue up 13% to INR7,481 crore; EBITDA up 41% to INR276 crore with margin at 3.68%.
539725|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 13% YoY to INR7,481 crore, with EBITDA including other income up 41% to INR276 crore and margin up about 74 bps to 3.68%. PAT rose 40% to INR150 crore, and H1 PAT grew 54% to INR274 crore on 10% revenue growth. Management attributed the growth mainly to better price realisations, with no volume growth expected this year as capacity is fully utilised. A 24 September 2026 change in edible oil import duties deferred trade purchases in September, lifting closing inventory, which management called a timing effect. This was the company's first earnings call, held to start a regular investor engagement.

demand_pricing: Management attributed the 13% Q2 revenue growth mainly to better price realisations; commodity prices rose 15% to 20%, and realisations track market prices.
Edible oil import duties revised effective 24 September 2026; trade deferred purchases in September, raising closing inventory. Management views this as temporary, with channel activity normalising.
Hedging: inventory largely sold through back-to-back physical forwards or hedged on CBOT and Malaysian exchanges; import payments hedged via forwards; open inventory held at 10% to 15%.

539807|2026-06.headline: Gross revenue rose 109% YoY to INR 2,680 crore and PAT rose 45% to INR 85 crore, while net revenue fell 3% to INR 147 crore.

539871|2026-06.headline: Thyrocare Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24.3% YoY to INR240 crores, with EBITDA margin at 32.2% and PAT of INR51.3 crores (+34%).
539871|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR240 crores (+24.3% YoY) and standalone revenue INR225.6 crores (+26.1% YoY), led by pathology growth of about 26%. Gross margin expanded more than 290 bps to 74.1% on better negotiations, 28% task volume growth and operating efficiency. EBITDA grew 34% to a 32.2% margin and PAT rose 34% to INR51.3 crores. Management formally launched specialty diagnostics commercially (allergy and genomics), announced plans to divest the nuclear imaging business, and restated test volumes to exclude calculated parameters.

segments.name: Pathology - franchisee

segments.name: Pathology - partnership (B2B/B2C)

segments.commentary: Revenue doubled YoY in the quarter, per management.

Franchisee network grew to about 11,700 active franchisees, a fourfold increase since the FY21 takeover. Field team roughly doubled over the year, from about 35-40 to about 70.

Specialty pricing: NIPT priced at less than half of competitors' prices; management aims for affordability and volume.

qa_highlights.answer: Nuclear business has not grown or been invested in; process expected to take about 6 months, with no definitive buyer yet.

539871|2026-09.headline: Thyrocare Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 25% YoY to INR271 crore, with a one-time INR45 crore NHL impairment weighing on reported profit.
539871|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 25% YoY to INR271 crore and standalone revenue grew 26.7% to INR256 crore, with pathology up 27%. EBITDA margin was 33% and PAT before exceptions rose 26% to INR60 crore. Management is exiting radiology subsidiary Nueclear Healthcare (NHL) by selling it to Trovera for INR141 crore, and booked a non-cash impairment of INR45 crore consolidated (INR9 crore standalone). Management is also launching specialty diagnostics and a pregnancy test kit, both of which are margin-dilutive near term.

segments.commentary: Being sold to Trovera for INR141 crore (INR81.9 crore cash plus INR59.5 crore equity), subject to shareholder approval. NHL degrew about 9% over the past 5 quarters, and its ROCE is 6.95% vs Thyrocare's 34.9%.

539872|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11.3% YoY to INR165.6 crore with gross margin up 210 bps to 48.3%; management guides 10-15% revenue growth for FY27.
539872|2026-06.overview: Bajaj Healthcare reported Q1 FY27 revenue of INR165.6 crore, up 11.3% YoY and 8.2% QoQ, with EBITDA of about INR29.6 crore (17.8% margin) and PAT from continuing operations of INR13.9 crore (8.4% margin). Domestic API was the main growth driver at INR92.3 crore (up 27% YoY), while exports (INR50.1 crore) and formulations (INR23.3 crore) contributed the rest. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 10-15% and EBITDA margins of 18-20% for FY27 and FY28, and reiterated pipeline timelines for peptide, oncology API, and CDMO/novel-drug launches. Receivable days fell to 131 from 145 at FY26 end, and the call was the company's first earnings call.

segments.name: Domestic API
segments.commentary: Revenue INR92.3 crore, up 27% YoY; management said API prices were broadly stable QoQ and the growth was not price-led. Ascorbic acid and salts contribute about 8-10% of revenue.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Revenue INR50.1 crore in Q1. Magnesium L-Threonate (nutraceutical ingredient supplied to a US innovator) is the largest export product at about 10% of FY26 revenue, with FY27 growth guided at 15-20%. Management expects export share to rise to 30-35% over time.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR23.3 crore in Q1. Cenobamate CDMO launch expected to add INR10-12 crore in FY27; Oncocare brand business covers 15+ brands across 23 states and 3 UTs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of 10-15% YoY; profit growth guided at a similar rate. FY28 top-line growth also guided at a similar rate.
EBITDA margin of 18-20% for FY27 and FY28.
Capex of INR40-50 crore every year over the next few years.

Receivable days expected to settle at 110-120 days going forward.

Oncology API dedicated facility: commercial target Q4 2028.
Gen Rx Pharmaceutical facility in Nashik (solid dosage forms): acquisition pending NCLT approval; commercial production expected in H2 2027.
Savli DSIR-approved R&D centre expansion of over 10,000 sq ft, expected to be operational by August 2026, housing 100+ researchers. R&D spend rose from 0.4% of sales in 2024 to 2.2% in 2026.
Three loss-making Tarapur plants: one sold, two remain with no buyer yet; sale proceeds not quantified.

Suvorexant: BE studies completed; commercialisation expected Q4 FY28 because the patent is still in force.

Vitamin C is about 8-9% of revenue; backward integration via ICT MoU expected to complete in 2029. Eight to ten API molecules being backward-integrated, expected to be 20-25% of revenue, with a 1-2% margin uplift.

539872|2026-09.headline: Bajaj Healthcare Q2 FY27 revenue rose 18.9% YoY to INR175.9 crores and PAT 26.9% to INR14.1 crores, with formulations up 82%.
539872|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations grew 18.9% YoY to INR175.9 crores in Q2 FY27 and 6.2% QoQ, with H1 revenue up 15.1% to INR341.5 crores. EBITDA rose 12.2% YoY to INR32.1 crores at an 18.2% margin, while gross margin fell to 48.3% amid West Asia disruption. Formulations (INR41.7 crores, up 82% YoY) and export API (INR62.6 crores, up 28.5%) offset a weaker domestic API line (INR71.6 crores, down from INR76.3 crores). Management reiterated FY29 targets of INR900-1,000 crores revenue and 18-21% EBITDA margin, and flagged higher inventory held as a precaution against Gulf disruption.

segments.name: Domestic API
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR71.6 crores vs INR92 crores in Q1 and INR76.3 crores a year ago; H1 up 10.1% YoY to INR163.9 crores. Management expects little pricing improvement over time.

segments.name: Export API
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR62.6 crores, up 28.5% YoY; Magnesium L-Threonate supplied to a US patent holder contributes about 11-12% of total turnover.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR41.7 crores, up about 82% YoY, driven by the Cenobamate API tablet launch in September through eight marketing partners; formulations are about 24% of revenue in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY29 target: revenue of INR900-1,000 crores with EBITDA margin of 18-21%.
Management said it is on track for the earlier guidance of 10-15% revenue and profit growth with 18-20% margin; Q2 growth was almost 20%.
Operating cash flow expected to be more than INR30 crores for FY27.
Total FY27 capex expected at INR65-80 crores; about INR50-60 crores per year thereafter to reach INR1,000 crores revenue.
Management expects gross margin and EBITDA margin to be maintained in coming quarters, supported by product mix.

Genrx (acquired, NCLT approved): INR200-250 crores revenue potential in two to three years. Oncology API plant: about INR200 crores in two to three years after commissioning in Q2 FY28. Peptide facility: first-year revenue INR70-100 crores in FY28-29.
capex_capacity: Peptide manufacturing plant (250 kg per annum, solid-phase synthesis and fermentation) scheduled for completion by 31 March 2027.
Oncology API plant to commence in Q2 FY28.
Dedicated formulation plant at Nashik (solid oral dosage, nasal, oral oncology, nutraceutical, ointment) expected operational in Q1 FY28.
New R&D centre started in August with over 80 staff, planned capacity of 120 chemists; R&D spend raised to about 2.5-3% of revenue.
Genrx acquisition to handle non-Baroda formulation volumes; new molecules to be made at Baroda, which is an approved facility.
demand_pricing: Cenobamate API tablets approved by DCGI (first in India, six strengths), launched commercially in September 2026; repeat orders received from partners, but secondary sales not yet known.

Regulatory filings: 110 DMFs filed, with approvals taking two to three years; 8 CEPs approved and 4 under review in Europe; 17 products registered with KDMF in South Korea; 3 products registered in Egypt with 10 more planned; 17 products identified for Brazil CBPF submission.
API pricing described as under pressure with little prospect of improvement; management said prices are more or less stabilised but volatile given Gulf disputes, freight and interest rates.
Management expects 60-70% of the portfolio to be backward integrated in two to three years.
Mix target over three to four years: formulations 45-50% and API 50-55% (vs about 20-24% formulations today).

qa_highlights.question: Will Manjusar formulation production shift to Genrx, and what is the role of the Nashik facility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Nashik is a strategic capacity addition for the next two to three years; new molecules will be made at the approved Baroda facility, and Genrx will handle other formulations for different markets.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital inventory rise and will it normalise by year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the higher inventory is a deliberate policy decision to avoid stoppages from the Gulf dispute; management did not give a normalisation timeline.

qa_highlights.question: What are the revenue potentials from Genrx and the oncology API plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Genrx: INR200-250 crores in two to three years after start-up. Oncology API plant: about INR200 crores in two to three years after it is in operation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex and is guidance on track?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex INR65-80 crores; CFO said the company is on track for the earlier 10-15% growth and 18-20% margin guidance, with Q2 growth near 20%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the operating cash flow outlook, given weak H1 conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating cash flow expected above INR30 crores for FY27; Q2 operating cash flow about INR15 crores; receivable days improved from 145 to 135.

qa_highlights.question: How is EBITDA margin holding up despite a roughly 225-250 bp YoY gross margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed stable EBITDA margin to product mix: export and formulation (Cenobamate launch) offset the domestic API dip, and said margins are expected to be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the portfolio can be backward integrated, and what are the margin effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 60-70% of products could be backward integrated in two to three years, with revenue from these products rising about 10-15% and margins improving; no specific margin figure was given.

risks_watch: Gross margin fell YoY (about 225-250 bp per analyst) amid West Asia/Gulf disruption, freight and interest-rate pressure; management expects improvement but gave no figure.

Domestic API revenue fell QoQ and YoY in Q2; API prices described as under pressure.
Commercial timelines: DMF/CEP approvals take 1-3 years; peptide and oncology plants depend on approvals with customers (6-10 months post-commissioning).
Cenobamate secondary sales not disclosed; management could not quantify FY27/FY28 revenue from it.
Execution risk from several new plants (peptide by March 2027, Nashik Q1 FY28, oncology Q2 FY28) and rapid senior hiring; management cited facilities as the main bottleneck over three years.

539876|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 11% YoY to Rs 2,283 Cr, with EBIT margin exiting near 10% versus 6.8% in H1.
539876|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 11% YoY to Rs 2,283 Cr, led by 10% growth in ECD and 14% growth in lighting. Management said EBIT margin improved from 6.8% in H1 to about 10% in Q4, driven by operating leverage, premiumisation, pricing and cost optimisation. Consolidated EBITDA was Rs 271 Cr (11.9% margin). Butterfly returned to double-digit revenue and profit growth, and management took an impairment on its Butterfly carrying value, which is non-cash but hits ROCE and asset turnover. Management also announced a new super-premium product line, Crompton Rhion, and an identical dividend to last year.

financial_highlights.change: YoY, Q4; management called it industry-leading
YoY, Q4, with steady EBIT margins
Management says Butterfly is now cash flow positive

segments.name: ECD (Electrical Consumer Durables)
segments.commentary: Q4 growth of 10%, broad-based across pumps, small domestic appliances and fans. Fans saw record March volumes; BLDC portfolio growing 30%-plus. Management says it gained share in every ECD product in FY26 but did not give category numbers.

segments.name: Small domestic appliances (SDA)
segments.commentary: Management said FY26 growth was in the early 20s percent and Q4 growth close to 30%, with a step-up in profitability. New launches included infrared cooktops, air fryers and premium juicers.

segments.name: Lighting (B2B and B2C)
segments.commentary: Q4 growth of 14%. Government share of B2B mix fell about 500 bps in FY26. Y-o-Y margin said to be roughly flat despite materially higher ad spend in the quarter.

segments.name: Butterfly Gandhimathi
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up 17% with steady EBIT margins and higher advertising spend. Management says it is back to strong double-digit growth in both revenue and profit, and an impairment was taken on its carrying value.

segments.commentary: Solar pumps revenue was about Rs 200 Cr last year and grew significantly this year. Rooftop order book is about Rs 500 Cr (about 38,000 units in Andhra plus Telangana), with about 5,000 homes installed so far. Management targets a Rs 2,000 Cr solar business in 3-4 years (corrected from Rs 1,500 Cr).

segments.name: Wires (Crompton Armor)
segments.commentary: Launched in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka and now selling in South India; national rollout is planned over the year rather than all at once.

guidance_outlook: Management expects margins to recover over time as input-cost turbulence from the war eases, but would not give a timeline.
Management said further material cost inflation came in April; it plans to offset this through pricing and Unnati cost actions, and says some benefits could be back-ended.
Dividend declared identical to last year.
Solar business aspiration: Rs 2,000 Cr over 3-4 years (management corrected the figure from Rs 1,500 Cr).
Butterfly will focus on gaining traction in North, East, West (NEW) markets in the coming year.
Water heater BEE norms from July: management said it is fully prepared, with some cost increase to mitigate or pass on.
capex_capacity: Annual R&D and innovation spend about Rs 100 Cr, per management.
Rhion super-premium PL created; the Large Kitchen Appliance business folds into it; about 70 EBOs already operating.
Lighting supply chain restructured: Baddi unit restructured earlier, Baroda cost base reset with VRS.
Wires rollout ramping from Tamil Nadu and Karnataka to other states over the year.
Solar rooftop execution stepped up in the last 2-3 months.
demand_pricing: Two price increases in ECD since the war began, ahead of competition; about 7-8% cumulative price increase in fans in FY26, mostly taken in Q4.
Management said cost inflation continued into April; a war room tracks costs weekly or daily.
Butterfly has taken price increases similar to ECD's.
Residential pumps demand was tepid due to heavy rain; management says it held share. Agricultural pumps grew in the teens after product launches.
Air cooler inventory was cleared in the season; management says it gained marginal share. Water heaters were among the top 2 players in GT, now said to be No. 2.
Management says traditional-trade debtors are flat YoY and solar pump collections are on expectation; no stress seen so far in builders or contractors.

qa_highlights.question: What price increases were taken against the cost inflation, and how much has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Two ECD price increases since the war began, ahead of competition; about 7-8% cumulative in fans in FY26, mostly in Q4, which offset material inflation. Further inflation came in April, and management is waiting to see before deciding pricing for the rest of Q1 and Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 contribution and FY27 ramp-up from solar pumps and rooftops?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar pumps grew from about Rs 20 Cr three years ago to about Rs 200 Cr last year, and grew strongly again this year. Rooftop order book is about Rs 500 Cr, with about 5,000 homes installed. Management declined to give an FY27 contribution estimate.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lighting margins dip, and is growth troughing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins were roughly flat YoY despite higher ad spend. Growth came from a shift away from government B2B contracts (down about 500 bps), a higher-ASP B2C mix (panels, floodlights) and a reset supply chain and cost base.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Butterfly impairment's tax impact and is the merger still planned?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said there is no tax angle and it is an accounting impairment, not a write-off. Management said the impairment is unrelated to the merger plan, which remains on the cards at the right time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the national rollout plan for wires?
qa_highlights.answer: Launched in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, with ramp-up across the country over the year and distribution via the full Crompton network. No specific revenue targets given.

qa_highlights.question: Is there channel or payment stress in the value chain?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said traditional-trade debtors are flat YoY, solar pump collections are on track, and FY26 operating cash flow crossed Rs 500 Cr. Management said builder and contractor exposure is small and no stress is seen so far.

Butterfly impairment hits ROCE and asset turnover; watch Butterfly growth in NEW markets outside the South.
Water heater BEE norms from July may add cost and pressure margins in LDA.

No ECD category breakdown or new-segment revenue disclosure, so growth contribution is hard to verify.
Rhion go-to-market and sourcing details still undisclosed.

Management attributed the quarter to commodity cost and availability disruptions, which led to about Rs 200 crore of lost primary sales, mainly in fans and partly in lighting. 539876|2026-09.headline: Crompton Q2 FY27 revenue rose 18.2% YoY to Rs 2,263 Cr and EBITDA 24.1% to Rs 205 Cr, with margin up 40 bps to 9%.

Revenue rose 18.2% YoY to Rs 2,263 Cr and EBITDA rose 24.1% YoY to Rs 205 Cr at a 9% margin. PBT excluding exceptional items grew 36.2%; the prior-year quarter carried a Rs 20 Cr Baroda plant restructuring exceptional, which inflates reported PAT growth of 65%. Management said price increases of about 80% of cost inflation have been passed through, supply disruptions from Q1 are over, and inventory days are back to year-ago levels. E-commerce was subdued due to a channel repositioning, and A&P spend was lower in H1.

539957|2026-03.headline: MGL Q4 FY26 net profit fell to INR132 crore from INR202 crore QoQ as West Asia LNG disruption curtailed industrial supply to about 80%.

539978|2026-03.headline: Quess Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose 28% YoY to INR 86 crore at a 2.2% margin on 6% revenue growth; FY26 margin crossed 2%.

540005|2026-09.headline: LTM Q2 FY27 revenue rose 5.1% YoY in constant currency to USD 1.24bn, with order inflow of USD 1.3bn and EBIT margin at 15.6%.
540005|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was USD 1.235bn, up 1.1% QoQ and 5.1% YoY in constant currency, with INR revenue of Rs 11,808 crores (+13.6% YoY). EBIT margin expanded 10bps QoQ to 15.6%, while PAT margin fell to 11.7% from 12.7% because Q1 included a one-time gain on Voicing.AI. Cash conversion weakened sharply (OCF/PAT 39%, FCF/PAT 24%) due to gratuity funding under the labour codes, an ad hoc TDS timing effect, and advance tax. Order inflow of USD 1.3bn was AI-centric, short-tenure deals, and management is deliberately shifting KPIs away from TCV. Management reiterated that H2 will be better than H1, with the Saudi business (routed via a JV and classified under Tech) a drag this quarter.

540025|2026-03.headline: Advanced Enzyme Q4 FY26 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 2,034 million, a record quarter, with EBITDA margin steady at 31%.
540025|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue reached INR 2,034 million (+22% YoY, +18% QoQ) and FY26 revenue reached INR 7,458 million (+17%), both record levels per management. EBITDA rose 39% YoY to INR 632 million at a 31% margin, and PAT rose 69% YoY to INR 453 million (22% margin). Human Healthcare, Animal Healthcare, Bioprocessing and Specialized Manufacturing all grew on a YoY basis, with Serratiopeptidase volumes a key driver. Management flagged input cost inflation (fuel, salt, solvents, packaging, logistics) and a challenging US market, and guided to steady margins and a double-digit growth aspiration for FY27 without quantified guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 120-130 crore capex to be spent in FY27 and what is the growth component?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed INR 123 crore for FY27, about INR 20 crore may slip to Q2; about INR 20 crore maintenance, INR 50 crore R&D facility, balance growth. Fermentation utilisation is around 70-75%, with a capacity decision next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why is US growth lagging the market, and what is the reason for the about 14% decline in international Human Nutrition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a weak US environment, the shift to branding most ingredients (which takes time), geopolitical issues, tariffs and hiring challenges; expects US growth of 8-10% at most at this juncture.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 growth reach 12%+ given the sales reversal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, it expects double-digit growth in the balance three quarters; the INR 10 crore incremental reversal (about 8% drag) is expected to come back in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Will the sales reversal normalise, and what caused it?
qa_highlights.answer: Export shipments were booked but still in transit at quarter end, so revenue was not recognised; the incremental reversal was INR 100 million over normal quarterly reversals and has already been recorded as of the call date.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 30% EBITDA margin achievable, and will energy costs ease?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins to return to about 30% and cited 30-32% as the target, with energy costs easing from Q2 through operational efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of novel food approval and the EFSA process?
qa_highlights.answer: Still under EFSA consideration; management said it could take three to six months, depending on authorities, and the process is on and off.

qa_highlights.question: Which new products and markets are driving future growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not track product-level sales; 15-20 molecules are in the pipeline, with expansion into biocatalysis, animal feed, ruminant, food, baking and detergent; bioenergy has no revenue yet and is deferred to after the new R&D facility next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital position at June 30, 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory about INR 190 crore, receivables about INR 131 crore, payables about INR 41 crore, net working capital about INR 280 crore; working capital cycle about 125-138 days.

540047|2026-03.headline: Dilip Buildcon FY26 consolidated PAT rose to INR1,398 crores on revenue down 20.6% to INR8,984 crores; FY26 order inflow INR18,548 crores.
540047|2026-03.overview: FY26 standalone revenue fell about 22% to INR7,005 crores, while standalone EBITDA dropped about 19% to INR734 crores and standalone PAT rose to INR841 crores from INR311 crores. Consolidated EBITDA was INR1,766 crores at a 19.6% margin. Management reframed the company into three verticals (EPC, MDO coal mining, and Assets/InvIT) and targets 75% of profit from long-term assets by FY29. Management guided FY27 standalone revenue growth of 30-40%, EBITDA margin of 11-12%, and INR10,000-12,000 crores of new orders, with net debt-free status targeted by FY28.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Builds assets for the group; FY26 order inflow INR18,548 crores and completions INR2,812 crores. Management targets INR10,000-12,000 crores of new orders in FY27 and 30-40% revenue growth.

segments.name: MDO (coal mining)
segments.commentary: FY26 coal production 28.72 million tonnes (Siarmal 22.35 Mt, Pachhwara 6.37 Mt). Revenue from mining about INR1,600 crores currently, guided to about INR2,500 crores in FY27, about INR3,100 crores in FY28 and about INR4,000 crores in FY29. Target 57 Mt by FY29.

segments.name: Assets / InvIT
segments.commentary: Holds about INR1,600 crores of InvIT units. Next tranche of 11 HAM assets expected to yield about INR1,800 crores of InvIT units for incremental investment of INR169 crores, with transfers through Q1 FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone revenue growth of 30-40% over FY26, supported by an order book of almost INR28,000 crores.
FY27 standalone EBITDA margin target of 11-12%.

Management expects about 75% of profit from long-term assets and 25% from EPC by FY29.

Transmission and solar projects: equity requirement about INR1,600 crores (solar about INR1,200 crores, transmission about INR400 crores); DBL targets 15% of equity with 85% from outside investors; transmission EBITDA margin above 24% and IRR in high teens; commissioning about 2 years from start.
capex_capacity: Siarmal coal handling plant capex pending; a revenue-share kicker applies once it reaches COD.
Pottangi mine to be set up over the next 3 years.

Under-construction projects of about INR1,000 crores plus invested, to be transferred to InvIT.

demand_pricing: Average monthly infrastructure tendering in FY26 was about INR1.4 trillion, below the government's FY26 target, due to state elections, regulatory scrutiny and administrative delays.

Bitumen and HSD (diesel) cost inflation from elevated crude prices; government contracts only partly pass this through via WPI/CPI-linked formulas, so some margin impact is expected, mainly in coal where HSD is a major cost.
Coal MDO pricing is contracted per tonne: about INR500 per tonne at Siarmal and about INR1,100 per tonne at Pachhwara.
Q4 mining margin fell temporarily because about 6 Mt of coal is stuck at Siarmal due to delayed government evacuation and rake unavailability.
Management stated 90% of the last 20 years' revenue came from national government and other states, and only 10% from the Madhya Pradesh state government.

qa_highlights.question: Will MDO revenue and profitability be shared quarterly, and what is the profitability outlook after the coal handling plant capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, MDO revenue and profitability will be shared quarterly. Revenue is projected at about INR2,500 crores in FY27 and INR4,000 crores by FY29, with similar margins to be assumed; no monetisation plan for the subsidiaries is announced.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected InvIT distribution after the transfers, given lower distributions from Alpha?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said transfer timing changed in FY26 and distributions are envisaged in slide 24; FY26 Shrem and Alpha dividend and interest income was INR64.5 crores, with total distributions close to INR100 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What are the equity structure, IRR and commissioning timeline for the transmission and solar projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Investors would put in about 85% of equity during construction with DBL 15%; transmission EBITDA margin above 24% and IRR high-teens for both. SPVs are formed, lender in-principle approvals obtained, and commissioning is about 2 years from start.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone receivables rise to INR1,783 crores despite lower revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR400 crores of Jal Jeevan Mission final 10% payments, which depend on hydro testing, are pending; they will be paid partly in Q1 and partly in Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How does coal margin trend, given FY25 blended margin around 26% vs 23% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed a 24-25% stabilised range is the right base, with improvement as volumes scale and the coal handling plant comes online.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a pass-through for the raw material escalation from the war?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts are linked to WPI and CPI, so pass-through is partial; NHBF is lobbying the government for relief.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of borrowing and what drives the interest cost trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Average cost of borrowing is about 9%; standalone interest cost fell 11% in FY26 mainly from working capital loan rates cut about 125 bps, partly offset by lower mobilisation advances.

risks_watch: About 6 Mt of coal stuck at Siarmal due to delayed evacuation and rake availability; margin normalisation depends on government logistics.
Raw material inflation (bitumen, HSD) with only partial pass-through under inflation formulas.
Execution of the transmission and solar equity structure depends on finding investors for 85% of INR1,600 crores equity; no investor named.
Receivables rose to INR1,783 crores; about INR400 crores of JJM payment pending hydro testing.
InvIT valuations depend on final BPC values, land handover and scope changes; InvIT unit values on balance sheet are about INR1,600 crores.
Delivery of the net debt-free goal by FY28 relies on InvIT transfers and mining cash flows.
Competitive intensity and high bidding in certain segments.

540047|2026-06.headline: DBL Q1 FY27 standalone revenue Rs 1,930 crore and EBITDA margin 10.32%; consolidated PAT fell to Rs 128 crore from Rs 271 crore.
540047|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue was Rs 1,930 crore with EBITDA of Rs 199 crore (10.32% margin, up from 10.11%), and standalone PBT rose about 26% YoY to Rs 72 crore. Standalone PAT fell to Rs 39 crore from Rs 123 crore, but the base quarter included a Rs 98 crore divestment gain. Consolidated revenue dipped to Rs 2,378 crore from Rs 2,620 crore, with consolidated EBITDA of Rs 429 crore (18.05% margin). Management reiterated FY27 guidance (revenue growth 30-40%, EBITDA margin 10-12%, debt reduction Rs 600-800 crore) and announced a stake sale in under-construction transmission and solar projects (about Rs 8,400 crore project cost) to Alpha Alternatives.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 11-12% remain unchanged, and will revenue growth be back-ended?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 10-12% margin guidance is unchanged. Revenue ramp-up starts in Q3, steps up in Q4 and continues into Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much bid value is pending opening, and what is the working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 15,000-20,000 crore of bids are yet to be opened. Working capital days are expected to fall to about 120 by year-end and about 90 next year, from 131-133 days now.

qa_highlights.question: Can MDO revenue reach the Rs 2,500 crore FY27 level given Rs 362 crore in Q1 and 4.79 MT output?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said coal output is on track: 27 MT at Siarmal and 7 MT at Pachhwara in FY27, with Q1 low due to evacuation and a PSPCL strike at Pachhwara. Siarmal coal fee is 78% until the CHP is ready, rising to 100%, with a major revenue jump expected in FY29. Full-year math given as about Rs 600/t for Siarmal and Rs 1,200/t for Pachhwara.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Rs 1,700-1,800 crore of InvIT units from the 11-asset tranche be realised, and can standalone dividends help cut debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Four assets flip in August, with COD for four done and three more by September. All 18 assets are targeted for transfer by FY27-end or Q1 FY28, subject to NHAI NOC after six months of the first annuity. Siarmal equity will be funded from internal accruals, and the bank has permitted use of accruals within the project.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Alpha Alternatives deal equity split, and is DBL's share ~Rs 800 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohan said total equity is about Rs 1,600 crore, with Alpha co-investing 49% (about Rs 800 crore). The remaining about Rs 800 crore comes from DBL and structured equity, with about Rs 900 crore of structured equity already raised. Structured equity is to be flipped into InvIT units at COD.

qa_highlights.question: What is the consolidated net debt trajectory, and is there a consol-level target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no consolidated net debt target. The focus is on standalone net-debt-positive by FY28, while consolidated debt will cycle as assets are built and transferred to InvIT. Rs 7,801 crore consol net debt is referenced; the company cites Rs 45,000 crore of road HAM projects done.

540048|2026-03.headline: S.P. Apparels Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue fell to INR 364 crore (from INR 399 crore) and EBITDA margin to 12.2%; management guides INR 2,000 crore FY27 revenue.
540048|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was soft on volumes: consolidated revenue declined year-on-year to INR 364 crore and EBITDA to INR 44 crore, with PAT down to INR 18.59 crore, as US tariff after-effects and shipping disruption delayed orders. Full-year consolidated revenue grew 13.2% to INR 1,578 crore and EBITDA rose 16% to INR 217 crore. Management says US orders are returning, guides to INR 2,000 crore consolidated revenue in FY27, and points to Sri Lanka ramp-up and EU/UK FTA benefits. Current utilisation is cited at 64%, and the timing of recovery in H2 FY27 is the key uncertainty.

segments.commentary: FY26 adjusted revenue INR 321.26 crore and adjusted EBITDA INR 49.23 crore; Q4 adjusted revenue INR 66.88 crore (vs INR 81.37 crore) and adjusted EBITDA INR 8.47 crore (vs INR 12.85 crore). Business is 100% US-customer based and was hit by tariffs.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue GBP 7.5 million (INR 87.04 crore) with positive EBITDA of INR 1.10 crore. Q4 revenue was INR 35.04 crore vs INR 18.34 crore a year earlier. Order book is GBP 6.1 million.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 71.54 crore (vs INR 79.41 crore); EBITDA loss narrowed to INR 6.1 crore from INR 6.84 crore. Management says Retail was EBITDA-positive from Q2 to Q4 FY26, and that finance cost, not depreciation, keeps it PAT-negative.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue target of INR 2,000 crore at 14-15% EBITDA margin (management said the 15% applies to the Garmenting division, not consolidated).
FY27 revenue split given as INR 1,800 crore Garmenting (incl. Young Brand and Sri Lanka), INR 150 crore SPUK, INR 80-90 crore Retail.
Core government export business targeted at 17-18% adjusted EBITDA margin as operating leverage improves.

Solar capacity target of about 4.5 MW by March 2027.
Possible contingent upside from customer reimbursement of tariff-related discount credits; not booked until received.
capex_capacity: India machines planned at 5,700 in FY27 versus the earlier 6,000 target; Sivakasi 440-machine expansion slowed due to US tariff uncertainty. Management said recruitment has restarted, with Sivakasi expected at 200-300 machines in about three months.
Sri Lanka: first factory operations began around mid-April 2026; scaling to four factories within 12 months; about 2,000 machines planned in FY27.

Salem (Young Brand) expansion of about 300 machines, worth INR 50-60 crore revenue, now expected to contribute in FY28 after about six months to commercial production; 1,400 Young Brand machines in FY27.
Adding 300 machines costs about INR 200-250 crore; management said capacity is not the constraint, people are.
Current utilisation is 64% in the quarter; management cites 90% as optimum. No further capacity expansion planned for FY28 until utilisation rises.
demand_pricing: Order book: SPAL Garmenting INR 380 crore, Young Brand INR 142 crore, SPUK GBP 6.1 million; total about INR 600 crore.
US customers returning with orders; management expects the pace to improve from August 2026. Lead time from order to shipment is 90-120 days.
Realisations stated as broadly intact; Q4 softness was volume-led rather than price-led. Raw material and yarn prices up about 5%; some pass-through to customers accepted.
Cotton price rose to about INR 75,000 per candle and has eased to about INR 70,000.

Rupee depreciation (about 95-96 per USD vs 90 earlier) is cited as helping competitiveness against Bangladesh and Sri Lanka, though CFO said 80% of orders are hedged on booking, so no direct pricing benefit is captured.

Management says customers are shifting orders from Bangladesh to India ahead of Bangladesh losing EU duty-free status by 2029; UK and EU FTAs expected within 2-3 months, with benefits mainly volume rather than price.
Group has 12 customers: about 4-5 US (incl. Young Brand) and 7-8 Europe/UK.

qa_highlights.question: Is rupee depreciation driving incremental volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said duty-paid status versus duty-free Bangladesh and Sri Lanka helps competitiveness and is bringing more business. The CFO added that 80% of orders are covered when booked, so there is no direct benefit from depreciation.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR 2,000 crore FY27 target be reached, given Sri Lanka and Sivakasi ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Sri Lanka FOB is about INR 45 crore in FY26, targeting INR 200-250 crore in FY27. Sivakasi adds about INR 40-50 crore, and H2 FY27 is expected to see the recovery as utilisation rises from 64%. Analyst arithmetic came to about INR 1,850 crore, and the gap was not fully bridged.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15% margin guidance on consolidated or Garmenting basis?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the 14-15% margin applies to consolidated figures in one answer, and later said the 15% applies to the Garmenting division only, with INR 2,000 crore on a consolidated basis. The basis is therefore ambiguous.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SPUK revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: SPUK has an order book of GBP 6 million and is targeting a further GBP 6-8 million for FY27, for GBP 12-14 million in total. Two anchor customers are each expected to give about GBP 8 million, and 2-3 more customers are being added.

qa_highlights.question: Will Retail become PAT positive?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said Retail is at EBITDA breakeven, and that finance cost on Retail Ventures is the drag. He said equity raising is needed and the company is ready to raise it now.

qa_highlights.question: Has labour returned after the capacity cut?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said workers left after the US capacity reduction, and that 30-40% have returned. Recruitment and training are ongoing, and management said this is not a labour disruption.

Labour re-hiring and training; only 30-40% of workers expected to return.

540048|2026-06.headline: S.P. Apparels Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA rose 15.9% to INR 61.4 crore on revenue flat at INR 401 crore; FY27 guidance of INR 2,000 crore reiterated.

PAT grew 20.4% to INR 24.9 crore. Management attributed the soft top line to U.S. tariff-related order holding in March-May and customer-requested shipment deferrals, and said growth will be back-end weighted into H2 FY27. The company reiterated its INR 2,000 crore FY27 revenue guidance, and announced a INR 3 per share dividend and a proposed stock split from INR 10 to INR 2 face value.

540061|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 35% YoY to INR 87 crore on 40% volume growth, but EBITDA margin was 7.36% and the company posted a net loss of about INR 1 crore.
540061|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 sales volume grew 40% YoY to 2,45,870 cubic metres and FY26 volume rose 37% to 8,26,904 cubic metres, with capacity utilisation climbing from 53% in Q1 to 78% in Q4. Revenue from operations was about INR 87 crore (up around 35% YoY) and EBITDA about INR 6 crore (margin 7.36%), but the company still reported a net loss of about INR 1 crore. For FY26, revenue was about INR 283 crore (up around 26%), EBITDA about INR 18 crore (6.21% margin) and net loss about INR 9 crore. Management attributed margin pressure to raw material and fuel cost increases, labour shortages and slow adoption of the new AAC wall panel product, which limited pass-through of cost increases.

financial_highlights.change: around 26% YoY vs INR 225 crore in FY25
FY25 margin about 13% per analyst question

segments.name: AAC blocks
segments.commentary: Management cited EBITDA margins of about 8% to 10% currently, with a peak of about 25% seen earlier; improvement expected over the next two to three quarters. Western India is the main focus.

segments.name: AAC wall panels
segments.commentary: Management guided gross margins of 50% to 60% and EBITDA margins of 30% to 45%. Full utilisation (80% to 85%) could generate revenue of about INR 100 to 125 crore. Adoption has been slower than expected.

segments.commentary: Management guided gross margins of 40% to 50% and EBITDA margins of 25% to 30%, with about INR 20 to 30 crore revenue from the newly installed plant. Bigbloc Building Ltd's plant at Umargaon began commercial production.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the FY26 margin decline (13% to about 6%) came from pricing versus cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 5% to 6 points came from pricing pressure and about 2 points from higher operating and manufacturing costs.

qa_highlights.answer: Target volume growth of 10% to 20%, led by Western India for AAC blocks and chemicals, with AAC panels growing nationally including bullet train station orders and Delhi and Bangalore targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Do you expect realisations to stabilise in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said realisations fell 5% to 7% over the last year and some cost increases have since been passed on; further pass-through is expected to lift realisations over the next two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How many carbon credits are held and what is the revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: About 150,000 tonnes of carbon credits are held, priced at about $2 to $3; issuance takes about three months before monetisation. No revenue or profit from carbon credits was recognised in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What margins and revenue can the AAC panel and construction chemicals businesses deliver?

qa_highlights.answer: Orders so far are about 40,000 to 50,000 square feet, contributing about 8 to 9 (unit as stated, likely million) to the order book.

540061|2026-06.headline: Bigbloc Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~40% YoY to ~INR 79 crore and EBITDA to ~INR 6 crore (~8% margin), with net loss narrowing to ~INR 70 lakh.
540061|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as an inflection point, with sales volume of 2,21,545 cubic meters (+32% YoY) and plant utilisation of about 69%. Revenue was about INR 79 crore (+~40% YoY) and EBITDA about INR 6 crore versus INR 1 crore a year earlier. The net loss narrowed to about INR 70 lakh from about INR 6 crore. Management said margin gains will come from utilisation (target 75%+), price hikes in some markets, and construction chemicals, and it deferred the Madhya Pradesh plant to FY28 commercial production.

segments.name: AAC blocks

segments.commentary: ~5% of Q1 revenue. Management describes it as a category-creation product with 30-35% EBITDA margin potential at higher utilisation; capacity can be expanded from 250,000 to 500,000 cbm with additional autoclaves. Projects cited include ITC, L&T bullet train stations and data-centre and metro talks.

segments.commentary: Mortar plant began operations in May 2026; Q1 utilisation about 20-25%, to be scaled over the next couple of quarters. Previously traded under the company brand via manufacturing partners.

540073|2026-03.headline: BLS International FY26 revenue rose 37% to INR2,998 crores and EBITDA 30% to INR819 crores, with Q4 PAT up 29% to INR187 crores.
540073|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the company's highest-ever year on revenue, EBITDA and PAT, driven by Visa application volumes, new contract wins and higher net revenue per application. Q4 FY26 revenue grew 18% to INR815 crores and EBITDA 17% to INR204 crores, with Visa & Consular volumes up 10% and Digital revenue up 36%. Digital EBITDA margins are thin (about 7-8%) after the Aadifidelis loan-distribution mix shift, while Visa & Consular margins expanded to about 40%. Management said the West Asia conflict has had a temporary impact on travel but has not dented annual growth, and guided to 20-25% growth on the FY26 base for FY27.

segments.name: Visa & Consular Services
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,840 crores (+11% from INR1,653 crores) and EBITDA INR738 crores (+30%), margin 40.1% vs 34.5%. Q4 revenue INR472 crores (+7%), EBITDA INR180 crores (+19%), margin 38%.

segments.name: Digital Services
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,158 crores (more than doubled from INR440 crores, +114%) and EBITDA INR81 crores (from INR60 crores), so margin is thin. Q4 revenue INR343 crores (from INR252 crores) and Q4 EBITDA INR24 crores. Growth came from BC/loan distribution (Aadifidelis, acquired Nov 2024) and assisted digital and citizen services.

guidance_outlook: FY27 internal target is 20-25% growth on an increased FY26 base, per Shikhar Aggarwal.

Management said Visa & Consular and Digital will both maintain current margins (about 40% and 7-8% EBITDA respectively), with Digital margins expected to improve over time as more services are implemented.
Management would not give April or Q1 FY27 trading commentary, saying only that business is 'steady' and growing over the same quarter last year.
Effective group tax rate is about 10-12%, possibly rising by about 1 percentage point if Dubai moves its tax rate from 9% to 12%.
Cash to be deployed for capacity expansion and inorganic growth; one acquisition announced and in pipeline, with a further INR2,000 crores of acquisitions mentioned over 4-5 years in an interview.
capex_capacity: UIDAI/Aadhaar passport-style service contract (about INR2,500 crores, 6 years, user-pay per application): Phase I of 40-50 offices rolled out; full rollout expected at 200+ offices, taking 1-1.5 years for full revenue; expected EBITDA margin 15-20%; contracted under BLS International, not E-Services.
Network of 155,000+ touch points and around 45,800 channel partners, described as asset-light.
China operations started about six months ago and are described as steady with further potential.
Management said no further acquisitions in the hotel space (UK hotel), with focus on asset-light models.
demand_pricing: Visa applications processed in FY26: 44.1 lakh vs 37.5 lakh (+18%). Q4 applications 10.8 lakh vs 9.8 lakh (+10%).

Q4 net revenue grew about 20% vs application growth of about 10%, due to higher value-added service conversion and new contracts at better pricing (Slovakia, Cyprus cited as newly deployed).
Business GTV on BC platform above INR1.1 lakh crores in FY26 vs INR87,000+ crores in FY25; leads worth INR36,800+ crores generated.
Management said the West Asia conflict has had a temporary impact on travel in some countries; March 2026 still grew vs March 2025, and FY26 annual growth was maintained.
Pipeline: management cited $1-2 billion of contracts expected to come up for bidding over the next one to two years, mostly in Europe and North America, with no split by stage given.
Major regions cited: UAE, Saudi Arabia, Morocco, Algeria, UK, USA, Canada, Singapore, and China (picking up).

qa_highlights.question: Has the West Asia situation hurt the last quarter, and would Q4 have been better without it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 EBITDA still grew 17% and FY26 EBITDA 30%, so the impact is temporary; it acknowledged some volume could have come back without the conflict. Q1 FY27 was not guided.

qa_highlights.question: Why did applications grow about 10% while Visa revenue grew only 7% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Sudhakar and Gaurav Chugh said net revenue grew about 20% against about 10% application growth, reflecting higher value-added service conversion and better pricing on new contracts; reported revenue is gross of third-party vendor sharing.

qa_highlights.question: How is April and FY27 revenue trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give April commentary and said it is growing steadily; internal FY27 target is 20-25% growth on the FY26 base.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capital allocation priorities for the INR1,434 crore net cash?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Amit Sudhakar said cash will go to expansion of existing business and inorganic growth; one acquisition is in the pipeline and a few more are under evaluation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organic vs inorganic split of growth?
qa_highlights.answer: No major new acquisition in FY26; Aadifidelis (acquired Nov 2024) contributed about 25% of revenue, and the rest is comparable with last year.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments are the acquisitions targeted at, and what is the Aadhaar contract economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisitions are being considered in both segments: Digital more domestic, Visa & Consular targeting overseas. The Aadhaar contract is too early to size; 15-20% EBITDA margin expected, over 6 years.

qa_highlights.question: Will Digital margins recover and can Visa margins of 40% be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Digital margins are 7-8% after Aadifidelis (loan distribution commission of 2-2.5%, with DSA pass-through), and have stabilised. Visa margins around 40% are to be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What is the effective tax rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Group effective rate about 10-12%; could rise about 1 point if Dubai's free-zone rate moves from 9% to 12%.

qa_highlights.question: Were the FX gain and intangible assets one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income was boosted by an INR5-6 crore FX gain, which is one-off; the rest is FD and debt mutual fund interest. Intangibles of about INR1,200 crores were tested by valuers with no impairment.

UIDAI contract ramp: full revenue depends on rolling out 200+ offices over 1-1.5 years; margins expected at 15-20%.

540073|2026-06.headline: BLS International Q1 FY27 revenue rose 25% to INR 891 crores, a record, with EBITDA of INR 252 crores (28.3% margin) and PAT of INR 202 crores.
540073|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was a record quarter for BLS on revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with growth coming from both Visa & Consular and Digital Services. Lakshya 31 five-year plan: 13%-15% USD CAGR and 16%-17% EBIT margin; 12.4% past 5-year CAGR includes SWC, per Rajeev Gupta.
Combined DSO expected at 85-90 days going forward.
Effective tax rate guided at 26.5%-27%.
