540205|2026-03.headline: Aditya Vision Q4 FY26 revenue rose 28% YoY to INR625 crore and PAT 36% to INR22 crore, despite a weak summer and FY26 PAT up only 11%.
540205|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 18% to INR2,672 crore and PAT grew 11% to INR117 crore, with EBITDA at INR228 crore (8.5% margin) and gross margin at 15.6%. Q4 was the strongest quarter, with revenue up 28% and same-store sales growth of 18%, though gross margin (16%) and EBITDA margin (8.1%) were lower than the prior year. Management said H2 is now as important as H1, reflecting a shift away from a seasonal model. Store count reached 207 across four states, with Chhattisgarh entered and Madhya Pradesh planned this year. Inventory was built up to about INR840 crore ahead of anticipated OEM supply constraints and BEE-driven price increases.

segments.name: Bihar
segments.commentary: Largest market at 74% of Q4 FY26 revenue and 75% of FY26 revenue; 118 stores across 38 districts.

segments.name: Uttar Pradesh
segments.commentary: 14% of Q4 and 13% of FY26 revenue; 53 stores covering 30 of 75 districts, with most new stores opened in Feb-Mar 2026 and contributing less than a full year.

segments.name: Jharkhand
segments.commentary: 12% of both Q4 and FY26 revenue; 33 stores covering 22 of 24 districts.

segments.name: Chhattisgarh
segments.commentary: Entered early with 3 stores covering 2 of 33 districts; no revenue split disclosed.

segments.name: Product categories
segments.commentary: Mobiles and laptops together exceed 25% of sales; ASP of mobiles rose about 20% in Q4, diluting gross margin. Small appliances grew about 50%, per analyst; cooling products (ACs, coolers, refrigerators) underperformed due to weak summer.

guidance_outlook: Management gives no formal store guidance; it cites about 25 stores when asked, and has added over 30 stores a year for the last 3-5 years.
Madhya Pradesh entry is on track for this financial year; Chhattisgarh and UP to be scaled up.
Management expects opex to grow in line with overall expenses rather than rise faster, as the store base becomes more mature.
Management cites an 8% to 10% EBITDA margin range as its endeavour, with 9% as a central target, but declined to give a timeline.
April 2026 described as very robust; May started colder but is expected to normalise into a normal summer.
No equity raise planned this financial year; internal accruals and working capital borrowings are expected to suffice.
capex_capacity: Store base reached 207 at March 31, 2026, after 102 stores were added in the last three years versus 105 in the prior 23-24 years.
Stores take 9 to 12 months to break even, per management.
Inventory of about INR840 crore held at end Q4 FY26, built ahead of OEM supply uncertainty (gas shortages linked to a Gulf conflict) and BEE-driven price increases of about 8% to 10%.
Plans to scale UP and Chhattisgarh while deepening Bihar and Jharkhand; a neighbouring state, previously held back by political uncertainty, is now being considered.
demand_pricing: Weak summer and extended rains hit H1; Q1 FY26 revenue grew 6% and H1 grew 11%. Q3 grew 28%, driven by festive demand.
Historically Q1 and Q2 contributed 55% to 60% of annual sales; management says this is now shifting towards a more balanced full-year model.
Price increases on mobiles and laptops lowered the margin mix; management said price hikes are not the main driver of profitability.
Management said OEMs bear the burden of unsold inventory and do not take returns; they help liquidate stock before new billing.
Real estate slowdown seen in Pune, Bengaluru and Hyderabad has not yet affected Bihar, UP or Jharkhand, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Will high inventory give a competitive and margin advantage over peers in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on peers' inventory and said it holds inventory as per its own strategy and historical levels, not to profit from price hikes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall about 100 bps YoY in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to weak cooling-product sales in H1 and a Q4 surge in low-margin mobiles (ASP up about 20%) and laptops (ASP up 8-10%), which together exceed 25% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 50% rise in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to brand ambassador onboarding, UP expansion, and variable costs such as freight, card commissions and dealer discounts that rise with the 18% volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: What are the normalised margins for mature Bihar, and when will UP match them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose state-wise margins, saying it aims to bring other states up to Bihar's level over time without sacrificing sales.

qa_highlights.question: What is the store expansion target for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal guidance given; management cited 25 stores when pressed and said it expects to keep beating its informal targets.

qa_highlights.question: When will EBITDA margin return to about 9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no timeline and pointed to an 8% to 10% margin range, with 9% as the central target, while not compromising sales growth.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from mix shift toward mobiles and laptops, whose ASPs are rising.
Q4 inventory build (about INR840 crore) exposes the company to price-cut and demand risk if the summer underperforms; May started colder than normal.
Cash conversion: management declined to guide on OCF/EBITDA, saying it depends on inventory and working capital.
Finance cost implies about 12.8-13% on average debt per analyst, but this includes lease liability interest; the bank borrowing rate was not disclosed.
Most UP stores opened in the last months of FY26, so UP contribution and unit economics are not yet visible on a full-year basis.
Opex rising faster than revenue in new geographies (UP, Chhattisgarh, MP) could weigh on EBITDA margins.

540212|2026-03.headline: TCI Express Q4 FY26 revenue rose 6% YoY to INR 327 crore, EBITDA margin 11.3%, PAT flat at INR 21 crore amid fuel and labour cost pressure.
540212|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew about 6% YoY to INR 327 crore and 4% QoQ, with total income of INR 331 crore. EBITDA rose 11% YoY to INR 37 crore (11.3% margin) while PAT was flat at INR 21 crore (6.3% margin). Full-year revenue grew about 2% to INR 1,236 crore, with PAT of INR 90 crore (7.2% margin). Management said the Gulf conflict pushed ATF prices up sharply and labour costs rose, and volume growth slowed to 4% YoY in Q4 after March.

segments.name: Surface Express
segments.commentary: Largest contributor; management said surface margin should improve with diesel-linked price pass-through, citing about 30% arbitrage. Surface grew in single digits in the last two quarters, with mid-single-digit to ~10% growth expected going forward.

segments.name: Multimodal (Air, Rail, C2C, e-commerce)
segments.commentary: About 18.5% of FY26 revenue, with management citing about 20% growth; target of 22% to 25% share over 2 to 3 years. Domestic and international air margins were hit this quarter, while rail and C2C margins were described as stable.

segments.name: Rail Express
segments.commentary: Management said rail gross profit is above 30% and realisation is about 2.5x surface. Rail volumes are not disclosed.

segments.name: E-commerce Express
segments.commentary: About 2.5% of business, with a target of 5%. Focus is on D2C and B2B merchant-to-warehouse movement with SME clients, not quick commerce.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guided at about 10% to 11%, with revenue growth of about 15% including price hikes.
FY27 margin improvement of 100 to 150 basis points at EBITDA and PAT levels, conditional on fuel prices stabilising.
Q1 FY27 volume expected at high single-digit growth, improving QoQ through the year.
Multimodal growth guided at about 20% in FY27.
Depreciation run-rate of INR 30 to 32 crore per year after ROU additions; about INR 6 to 6.25 crore per quarter.
Capex plan revised from INR 500 crore to INR 400 crore for FY23 to FY27; about INR 130 crore planned for FY27. A new five-year plan will follow.
Branch expansion of about 100 branches in FY27 (40 surface, 60 rail, air and C2C).
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation was about 83.25% in Q4, improved QoQ.
Nagpur sorting centre upgraded and now owned; semi-automated, about 70,000 to 75,000 sq ft, with only 5% to 7% change in cut-off time.
Ahmedabad and Kolkata sorting centres under construction, to finish in FY27, with automation ramping up in the first half of FY28. Lucknow also in progress.
Mumbai and Kolkata sorting centres moved to 5-year leases, which added ROU assets and raised depreciation.
Next sorting centres planned for Chennai and Bangalore.
demand_pricing: Management said diesel rose about INR 8 and the company is passing it on to customers, with 85% pass-through expected and 10% to 15% of customers still negotiating.
Air fuel (ATF) rose about 50% and international air rates went up 2x to 3x after the Gulf conflict began at end-February, leading customers to hold shipments in March.
Labour costs rose 15% to 20%, adding about 100 basis points to overall cost, per management.
SME share of revenue was 48% to 52% against a historical 50:50 split; management expects a return to 50%+ with the last two months' results described as good.
Revenue per kg is about INR 12.3 to 12.4 with EBITDA of about INR 1.25 to 1.27 per kg, against a historical INR 1.8 to 2.0 per kg, per an analyst's calculation.
The company expects to benefit from air-to-surface and rail shifts as higher air prices push customers to other modes.

qa_highlights.question: Why has growth been restricted and margins fallen from 15% to 16% to 10% to 11%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the Gulf war and ATF spike, airline consolidation, airport privatisation, lower truck utilisation and a 100 bps hit from labour costs. It guided FY27 PAT margin recovery of 100 to 150 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume and revenue guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth of about 10% to 11% and revenue growth of about 15% for FY27, with Q1 at high single digits and QoQ improvement after that.

qa_highlights.question: Is the multimodal segment margin dilutive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said air margins were temporarily hit by costs. Rail and C2C margins are stable and surface margin should improve with diesel pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the depreciation and interest increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Two sorting centres were moved to 5-year leases under Ind AS 116, which lifted ROU assets. Management said depreciation runs at about INR 6 to 6.25 crore per quarter. Pre-Ind AS EBITDA would have been about INR 29 crore, versus INR 32 crore reported, per the analyst's calculation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the e-commerce strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: E-commerce is about 2.5% of business, targeted to 5%, through D2C and B2B merchant-to-warehouse flows with SMEs and some aggregator platforms. Quick commerce is not in the strategy.

risks_watch: Further diesel increases beyond INR 8 could delay pass-through and compress margins, according to management.
Prolonged Gulf conflict may raise ATF prices, reduce air volumes and push costs up.
Labour cost inflation from minimum wage and social security norms, plus state-level pressure.
Rupee weakness raising input costs.
SME stress and the share of SME revenue, which fell to 48% to 52%.
Management has not disclosed non-surface volumes, which limits visibility on the rail and air business.

And obviously we have to be willing to bring back the double-digit margin on a PAT level because, again we don't have any cost and depreciation and interest on that part.

540212|2026-06.headline: TCI Express Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to INR 312 crore, with PAT up 6% to INR 22.4 crore and volumes up 7.5% to 2.5 lakh tonnes.
540212|2026-06.overview: Income from operations grew about 9% YoY to INR 312 crore and EBITDA rose 11% to INR 37 crore, with margin at 11.7% versus 11.5%. PAT rose 6% to INR 22.4 crore (7.1% margin). Management said the fuel price hike taken in mid-May was only partly reflected in Q1 (June only), so benefits should show from Q2. The company stated it is debt-free with net cash of about INR 118 crore.

financial_highlights.change: up ~6% YoY from INR 21 crore; margin 7.1%

segments.name: Surface Express
segments.commentary: Largest contributor; grew 9% YoY on existing customers, new accounts and industrial growth. Management targets accelerating to double-digit growth.

segments.name: Domestic Air Express
segments.commentary: Grew 29% YoY per opening remarks (CEO-level figure); later cited ~28% on enterprise account wins and airline partnerships.

segments.name: International Express
segments.commentary: Grew 27% YoY on new customers, win-backs and expanded global carrier partnerships.

540222|2026-03.headline: Laurus FY26 revenue rose 23% to INR6,813 crore and EBITDA margin hit 26.8%, with Q4 margin at 28.9%; FY27 capex guided to about INR3,000 crore over two years.
540222|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a strong year: revenue of INR6,813 crore (+23%), gross margin about 60.4%, EBITDA of INR1,826 crore (26.8% margin, +6.7 pp) and PAT of INR889 crore (+148%). Q4 revenue grew only 5% YoY to INR1,812 crore, but Q4 EBITDA margin reached 28.9% on operating leverage and better mix. CDMO grew about 38% in small molecules to INR1,896 crore, while Affordable Medicines (formerly Generics) grew 18% to INR4,733 crore. Management raised its multi-year capex expectation sharply, to around INR3,000 crore over the next two years from the earlier INR1,000 crore a year reference, and the call stressed CDMO share rising to 50% by FY30.

segments.name: Small molecule CDMO
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR1,896 crore (+38%); Q4 sales about INR524 crore. Growth came from late-stage programs, commercial NCE API supplies and ramp-up of growth projects.

segments.name: Total CDMO (incl. Bio)
segments.commentary: Full-year CDMO business a little over INR2,000 crore (INR2,080 crore), above 30% of revenue versus 13% six years ago.

segments.name: Laurus Bio
segments.commentary: Q4 sales about INR65 crore (+124% YoY on a low base); FY26 sales up about 15%. Phase 1 fermentation capacity at Vizag due by end-2026.

segments.name: Affordable Medicines (formerly Generics)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,223 crore with growth moderating; FY26 revenue INR4,733 crore (+18%), driven by ARV and oncology volumes and developed-market launches.

segments.name: ARV
segments.commentary: FY26 ARV revenue about INR2,800 crore, versus the INR2,500 crore plus or minus 200 crore run-rate previously cited; ARV now 41% of revenue, down from 67% six years ago. Mix is about two-thirds API and one-third formulations.

guidance_outlook: Capex guidance raised to about INR3,000 crore over the next two years, from the INR1,000 crore a year reference; one analyst's question cited INR1,500 crore a year.
Gross debt may rise slightly in FY27, but debt/EBITDA is expected to hold at or soften from 1.25x.
Effective tax rate around 25-26%; standalone at 25%.

Expects good YoY CDMO growth in FY27 with possible quarter-to-quarter lumpiness; Affordable Medicines order book in place for strong FY27 growth, with no quantitative guidance.
CDMO expected to reach 50% of sales by FY30; ARV revenue stays around INR2,800 crore but its share falls.
R&D spend to stay around 4.1% of sales in FY27.
capex_capacity: Unit 7 greenfield manufacturing: first production ready for commercial validation by March 2027; four more manufacturing units in FY28, adding over 2,000 cubic metres of reactor volume.
Commercial-scale peptide manufacturing block ready for validation in Q2 FY27; management declined to give peptide capex or capacity numbers.

Laurus Bio fermentation greenfield at Vizag: Phase 1 operational by end-2026. Bangalore R2 is fully occupied (4 x 45,000 litre fermenters); 250,000 litres now, another 400,000 litres by year-end, with room for 600,000 more.
KRKA JV formulation facility in Hyderabad: Phase 1 by mid-2027.
Formulation capacity up 20% to 12 billion units in FY26; a new tertiary packaging/formulation facility is due in June for an existing 3-billion-tablet CMO partner.
Company exceeded 8,200 cubic metres of small-molecule reactor volume in FY26. Asset turnover 0.89x.
demand_pricing: ARV pricing was broadly constant in FY26; higher ARV sales were driven by full utilisation of ARV assets.
Gross margin gain was attributed to softer raw-material prices and process improvements, with better product mix.
Q4 saw some solvent price pressure, but management said production is not affected and it expects no disruption through June; some pressure expected, offset by higher utilisation.
Management said the three recent commercial APIs have multi-year patent life and partner forecasts, and it sees no destocking risk; it also said there is no single-product concentration.
Geopolitical disruption may pressure raw-material availability, logistics and OTIF performance across the industry.

qa_highlights.question: Is there product concentration or destocking risk in the CDMO book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said three commercial APIs delivered in the last 18 months have multi-year patent life and clear partner forecasts; no destocking seen and no single-product dependence.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating leverage drive margins beyond gross margin gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects operating leverage next year as capacity utilisation rises; Q4 EBITDA margin was near 29% and rose through each quarter of FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Vizag fermentation: yield variability and ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial Vizag batches are industrial chemicals, surfactants and polymers (non-pharma); contamination is the main risk, and products are moving from 45 KL to 110 KL fermenters after commercial gates were cleared.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ARV API/formulation split and non-ARV formulation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About two-thirds API and one-third formulations for FY26 overall; non-ARV formulations are growing with momentum expected into FY27 from existing products.

qa_highlights.question: Will ARV share fall, and what is the CDMO target?
qa_highlights.answer: ARV stays around INR2,800 crore in absolute terms but its share falls; CDMO is targeted at 50% of sales by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Why was capex raised, and what are return expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says capex is growth-led with visibility on customer and product, and expects about INR3,000 crore over two years.

Solvent and raw-material price pressure and geopolitical supply risk; management expects some pressure but claims stable margins.

540222|2026-06.headline: Laurus Labs Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29% to INR2,026 crores, with EBITDA margin at 31.8% and CDMO up 69% to INR835 crores.
540222|2026-06.overview: Revenue of INR2,026 crores grew 29% YoY, led by commercial supplies in CDMO and continued strength in Affordable Medicines. Gross margin was about 62.7% and EBITDA of INR644 crores at a 31.8% margin, up about 7 percentage points QoQ, as management attributed the gain to operating leverage and product mix. Profit after tax was about INR368 crores and ROCE about 19% versus 17.7% a year earlier. Management raised the FY27 capex guidance to about INR2,000 crores from INR1,500 crores, and net debt rose to INR2,656 crores with debt-to-EBITDA at 1.28x.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the increase reflects capacity needed for existing customers' programs, including advanced intermediates and API, and new modalities in small molecules, and is tied to specific near-term partner needs.

qa_highlights.question: What share of small-molecule CDMO revenue came from commercial supplies, and is the non-commercial share sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: About 55% came from commercial supplies; the remaining 45% is mainly Phase III supplies, with one program already approved and expected to turn commercial soon.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Krka JV capex and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR400 crores invested so far, with another INR400 crores needed, partly funded by a partner loan; oncology facility early next year and solid orals in H2 CY2027.

qa_highlights.question: Will CDMO margins improve, and what is the gross margin trend given raw material pressures?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin improved from 61% to 63% QoQ and was up about 3 percentage points YoY; management said margin pressure from global conflicts is not significant and expects similar margins going forward.

Management said the fundamentals were intact but flagged higher staff costs for capability build, a slowdown in same-store growth in mature metro stores, and heavy competitive pressure from quick commerce. Avenue E-commerce (DMart Ready) was narrowed to 11 cities after exits from seven cities, with its EBITDA falling about 43% and a net loss of INR307 crore. Management reiterated a roughly 15% internal store-addition target and did not disclose e-commerce KPIs.

financial_highlights.change: Roughly flat; gross margin +16 bps, employee cost +27 bps, other expenses -9 bps
Total debt incl. AS 116 INR2,267 crore
Retail business area ~20.6 million sq ft
Sales +17%; PBT -24%; net loss INR307 crore

segments.name: Avenue Supermarts (standalone DMart stores)
segments.commentary: Sales +~16% with gross margin up 16 bps to within the 14-15% range; employee cost up ~33% in standalone financials including wage code impact. Entered five new states in FY26.

segments.name: Avenue E-commerce (DMart Ready)
segments.commentary: Sales +17% but EBITDA down ~43% and net loss INR307 crore. Exited seven quick-commerce cities; now focused on 11 cities, with 165 pickup points cited. Contract labour cost +24% and transport +34%.

segments.name: Align Retail (grocery packing)
segments.commentary: Sales +~16.5% and PAT +~24%.

segments.name: Avenue Food Plaza (fast/ready food)
segments.commentary: Sales +~35.5%; returned to profit with PAT margin ~9% after prior-year losses from expansion.

guidance_outlook: Internal store-addition benchmark ~15% of store base annually; could run a few points higher or lower depending on real estate timing.
Same-store growth expected to hover around last financial year's level (~7.5-8%) for FY27 for older stores; no sharp increase expected, all else equal.
Long-term North Star: ~15% gross margin and ~5% net margin; no intention to expand margin at the cost of customer proposition.
Expect efficiency gains in AEL from consolidation to 11 cities in FY27 onwards, per AEL CEO.
Staff cost built ahead of volume growth; management says it is hard to say if the build-up has ended.
Plans to invest in ERP and wider technology upgrades; management expects only marginal near-term margin impact.
capex_capacity: FY26 store additions: 85, with 15 on long-term lease; 68 stores in total now on lease out of 500+.
Land-to-store conversion takes 2-3 years depending on store configuration; pipeline of projects covers the next 2-3 years.
Debt: CP outstanding ~INR800 crore; INR1,000 crore NCD approved, may take total borrowing to ~INR2,000 crore by year-end, mainly to fund capex and reduce cost of debt.
Warehouses added in FY26 raised inventory days to 33.2.
demand_pricing: Quick commerce competition intensifying in dense metros (Mumbai, Bangalore, Hyderabad) where mature stores are saturated; management cites capacity, saturation, high throughput and competition as reasons for slower metro SSSG.
Management says FMCG vendors are not shifting attention away from DMart; many are doubling down.
Management says monthly/bulk shopping in metros is stable and strong, with good traction in Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities; newer Tier 2/3 stores are doing better than older metro stores.
Pricing follows vendor pass-through; no pricing guidance given.
Quarterly growth was 13% (Dec-25 quarter, deflation in staples), 19% (Mar-26 quarter, panic buying), and 15% (Jun-26 quarter).

qa_highlights.question: Will SSSG recover to double-digit levels given quick-commerce and maturity pressures in metros?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SSSG is likely to hover around the current range (~7-8%) and not rise considerably, especially for older stores; new stores are opened nearby to reduce pressure on existing stores.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 15% store-addition target conservative and can it go to 100-150 stores a year?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal target is ~15%; capital and people are not constraints, and land acquisition, permissions and build time (2-3 years) are. Management said 100-150 stores is not a reasonable number at about 500 stores currently.

qa_highlights.question: What is the economics of leasing versus owning stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share lease vs owned economics; said both models work. 68 stores are on long leases and 15 of the 85 stores added in FY26 were leased. Niladri said PBT is a fair measure of lease impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the mix of AEL get cut to 11 cities and why not experiment with faster delivery?
qa_highlights.answer: Seven cities were exited because their contribution was minimal. Management said it will not pursue immediate delivery; it will prove the six-hour slotted model in 11 cities first because losses had grown with expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the rise in employee costs and why are contractual headcounts lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Permanent headcount rose ~4,000 (75-80% of additions are store-management cohorts). Frontline staff are non-permanent; productivity and mechanisation held down non-permanent headcount. Wage code from December 2025 also added costs.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add non-metro growth via quick commerce given Flipkart and Blinkit expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not see a risk of LFL falling below 5%; it sees organised retail still under-penetrated in smaller towns and has no point of view on QC adoption outside top cities.

risks_watch: Continued SSSG slowdown in mature metro stores (~7-8% range expected) as quick commerce and new nearby stores take share.
AEL profitability: EBITDA down ~43% with net loss INR307 crore; watch whether consolidation to 11 cities improves throughput and transport/labour costs in FY27.
Rising staff costs (employee cost +27 bps of sales, standalone employee expense up ~33%) with wage code impact and capability build.
Lower return ratios (ROE ~13.5%, ROCE ~17.1%) and rising debt to fund expansion; NCD plan of INR1,000 crore.
Store-addition pace (85 in FY26 vs ~15% target) depends on land and lease availability; slower ramp in new Tier 2/3 stores.
Management declined to disclose DMart Ready KPIs, store-level margins, lease economics, land value, and category-level data.

Management was evasive on specific metrics (e-commerce KPIs, lease economics, land value, pricing outlook), deferring with 'we don't disclose' responses.
key_quotes: The model that this business has of providing everyday low price through an everyday low-cost operation isn't just a strategy, but it also has become its moat and will continue to protect us for years to come.
So we do want to prove that this way of working is sustainable in these 11 cities first, and so we are channeling all our attention and resources in AEL towards this goal.
And so therefore, 15% kind of a gross margin and let's say around a 5% kind of a net margin should be the North Star for this business even in the future.

540401|2026-06.headline: Maximus Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 52% YoY to INR59.91 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 7.64% from 9.81% on Middle East war input costs.
540401|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR59.91 crores versus INR39.52 crores a year earlier, with EBITDA up about 18% to INR4.58 crores. Margin compression, attributed to higher input and freight costs from the ongoing Middle East war, and higher finance costs (INR1.53 crores vs INR0.92 crores) left PAT at INR2.05 crores versus INR2.33 crores a year ago. Management highlighted the proposed associate acquisition of Quebec Petroleum (40% stake), a Kenya grease plant planned for Q3 FY27, and a Tanzania warehousing expansion. Management guided to crossing about INR200 crores revenue in FY27 on a conservative basis.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Highest EBITDA margin among the three verticals (manufacturing, toll blending, trading) in Q1 FY27 and historically. Operations in UAE and Kenya.

segments.name: Toll blending
segments.commentary: Management says it is being pursued aggressively; in talks with an East African MNC for toll blending.

segments.name: Trading
segments.commentary: Lowest-margin vertical per management. Long-term target split: manufacturing plus toll blending 75-80%, trading 20-25%.

segments.name: Specialty lubricants
segments.commentary: Contribute around 40% of topline, per CFO.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue expected to cross about INR200 crores on a conservative basis, with healthy EBITDA margins (stated even under the ongoing war scenario).
Margins expected to hold at current levels or improve over the next couple of quarters if supply disruption persists, through product mix diversification.
Kenya grease manufacturing facility planned for commissioning in Q3 FY27.
Tanzania expansion: initially warehousing and distribution, moving to manufacturing once scale is reached.
Recently launched modernisation programme: automated batch blending, additional storage and warehousing, improved filling lines, and capacity expansion at UAE and Kenya plants.
Capacity considered sufficient for next 2-3 years on single-shift basis; additional storage capex needed for full utilisation.
capex_capacity: Combined manufacturing capacity of about 50,000 KL across UAE and Kenya plants.
Capacity utilisation at about 45% across both units.
Kenya grease plant to cater to East African market, which has few grease manufacturers; also to support toll blending.
Proposed acquisition of an additional manufacturing unit as an associate; process underway, details to be shared later.
Quebec Petroleum: associate investment with initial 40% stake, aimed at entering the Indian domestic market.
demand_pricing: Management says demand for lubricants is supported by industrialisation, infrastructure, vehicle ownership and mining, power and construction; customers are shifting toward premium and specialty products.
Cited Middle East and Africa lubricant market growing from about USD 9.1 billion (2024) to USD 12.4 billion (2034).
Company serves more than 400 customers across 25+ countries and 50+ industries.
Top 10 customers account for roughly 70-75% of revenue, including distributors; company sells mainly through distributors, not B2C.
Product prices and landed costs (freight, insurance) rose due to the Middle East war; company passed on a partial cost increase, which also raised receivables.
Base oil and white oil prices are positively correlated with crude, with a lagged and non-identical impact on lubricant prices.
In Kenya, incumbents Shell and Total have not changed payment terms despite new entrants.

qa_highlights.question: How sensitive are margins to base oil and crude price movements?
qa_highlights.answer: Not directly coupled but positively correlated; raw materials (base oils and white oils) move in the same direction with a lag and not in the same proportion.

qa_highlights.question: Current utilisation of the 50,000 KL capacity, and targets over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: About 45% utilised; capacity is sufficient for 2-3 years on a single shift, but full utilisation would need additional storage capex.

qa_highlights.question: Which vertical has the highest EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Manufacturing, both in Q1 FY27 and historically; toll blending is being pursued more aggressively.

qa_highlights.question: Share of premium and specialty versus conventional revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Specialty lubricants contribute around 40% of topline.

qa_highlights.question: Why have receivables risen faster than revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher topline (about 50% growth), higher product prices and landed costs from the war, and partial pass-through of cost increases to selling prices.

qa_highlights.question: What if supply disruption lasts more than six months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has onboarded new customers and broadened product baskets; margins may dip further but aim to hold or improve through diversification; still expects over INR200 crores revenue in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How will Quebec Petroleum contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Associate with 40% stake; its profits will be included in consolidated financials; focus is India domestic market, while Maximus covers Middle East, East and North Africa.

qa_highlights.question: Target revenue split between trading and toll blending over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Manufacturing plus toll blending 75-80%, trading 20-25%; split between manufacturing and toll blending not disclosed as they overlap in co-branding.

qa_highlights.question: Concentration of revenue and B2B versus B2C mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Top 10 customers about 70-75% of revenue (distributors included); no own retail outlets; major revenue comes via distribution channels.

risks_watch: Margin compression: EBITDA margin down about 217 bps YoY to 7.64% due to input and freight costs from the Middle East war.
Working capital: receivables rising faster than revenue; financial cost up about 65% YoY to INR1.53 crores.
Customer concentration: top 10 customers about 70-75% of revenue.
Quebec Petroleum associate acquisition and additional manufacturing unit acquisition: terms and financials not yet disclosed.
Competitive response in Kenya from incumbents such as Shell and Total; payment terms unchanged so far.
Management did not split revenue between manufacturing and toll blending; the reported Q1 PAT decline despite revenue growth needs monitoring.

540403|2026-03.headline: CL Educate revenue rose about 55% to ₹570 crore in FY26 and EBITDA more than doubled to ₹69 crore, driven by the DEXIT acquisition.
540403|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 as the first year the group crossed ₹500 crore revenue, with revenue up from ₹368 crore to ₹570 crore and EBITDA up from ₹33 crore to ₹69 crore. Cash generated from operations rose to ₹79 crore from ₹26 crore, and the acquisition-linked borrowing has been reduced from ₹210 crore to ₹180 crore. The DEXIT (assessments) integration is described as complete. The L&D/EdTech segment remains under structural pressure, with realisations down 12-14% and revenue down about 11%, and management expects it to stay flat for roughly four more quarters. Fundraising has been put on a slight pause.

financial_highlights.change: acquisition debt reduced to ₹180 crore from ₹210 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and bank balance (as on date)
financial_highlights.change: from about ₹50 crore last year, excluding ₹185-190 crore pending RPS redemption

segments.name: Assessments (DEXIT)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose to ₹223 crore from ₹205 crore and EBITDA to about ₹51 crore from ₹34 crore. All existing contracts were rolled over and 20 new customers were added. FY27 order book is about 80-85% of FY26 revenue, per management.

segments.name: L&D / EdTech (test prep, university engagement, publishing)
segments.commentary: Enrollment volume grew about 4% but average realisation fell 12-14%, so revenue declined about 11%. Management expects revenue to stay roughly flat for about four quarters, with profitability improving from Q1 FY27 after cost recalibration.

segments.name: MarTech (Kestone, events, VOSMOS, VIRSA)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 11% to about ₹161 crore: international up about 20%, India up about 5%. EBITDA was slightly lower due to set-up costs for the new social events and luxury wedding business. Domestic to international mix is about 1:2.

guidance_outlook: Assessments: management expects reasonably healthy revenue growth in FY27, backed by an order book of about 80-85% of FY26 revenue six weeks into the year.

MarTech: shift to higher-margin CEP and VOSMOS/VIRSA products over 12-18 months; pruning low-margin MMS and pass-through businesses.
Discontinued operations: bulk of losses done, with a little residual impact possible in Q1 FY27 and none expected beyond that.
Talevate: target to sign 8-10 corporates and about 100 jobs over the next few quarters, testing the MVP before scaling.
capex_capacity: Working capital is about 50% of revenue despite about 50% revenue growth, per management.
Management is marketing land assets, including a Raipur plot earmarked for a school, and is seeking a buyer at the right price.

Remote proctoring and BYOD technology is being built out at DEXIT; the mySathi IP platform has started going to market.
Settlement of ₹185-190 crore RPS amount awaits NCLT capital reduction approval; order reserved, next hearing on May 15, 2026.
demand_pricing: L&D: enrollment volume up about 4%, but realisation down 12-14%. Students are shifting from ₹30,000-60,000 full programmes to ₹2,000-4,000 modular components.
MBA revenue expected flat to slightly down, with volumes rising. UG segments (law, BBA, IPM) are holding or raising prices, and growth is expected there.
Assessments: government contracts are about 40-45% of mix and private 55-60%. Pricing is similar across both and the market is price-sensitive.
Assessments: rollover of exam dates by 60-120 days shifted some FY26 revenue into FY27.
Competition: PhysicsWallah-type players are seen as low-price and not a direct threat; management launched products at about 50% above PhysicsWallah pricing and one-third of regular prices.

qa_highlights.question: Does the NEET controversy open opportunities for DEXIT in nationwide exams?
qa_highlights.answer: Yatrik Vin said it is a significant opportunity; DEXIT already conducts exams for IRDAI, ICAI and NISM, and its digital and surveillance tech is ready.

qa_highlights.question: What is the DEXIT government/private mix, contract duration, and government tender criteria?
qa_highlights.answer: Government is about 40-45% and private 55-60%. Contract tenure varies from one to five years, or order-based. RFPs weigh technical at 65-70% and commercial at 30-35%.

qa_highlights.question: How does the order book work, and why is it not 100% revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says 80-85% coverage is in hand for FY27, and sales efforts target a higher rollover. Exam timing set by clients can push revenue into the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the fundraising plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Satya Narayanan said fundraising is on a slight pause given the environment, and the boards want value at the right valuation. Updates are expected in the next quarter or two.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the cash and current liabilities linked to NSE?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹182 crore was left behind from the NSEIT transition and has earned ₹11-12 crore of interest, so about ₹193-194 crore is on the balance sheet. It will be knocked off against RPS after NCLT approval and moved from non-current to current liabilities.

qa_highlights.question: How will VIRSA affect MarTech in North America?
qa_highlights.answer: Pilots with Salesforce, Dell and Infosys have had positive feedback. The Salesforce work is for Canada, with a scale-up to the US expected over the next couple of quarters.

540403|2026-06.headline: CL Educate Q1 FY27: revenue fell about ₹17.5 crore QoQ-type decline offset by ₹18 crore cost cuts, lifting EBITDA margin ~218 bps to 16.6%, though still loss-making after tax.
540403|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 revenue was weak, with a decline of about ₹17.5 crore on a full-quarter basis, but operational and overhead cost cuts of about ₹18 crore (₹9.3 crore service delivery, ₹8.7 crore fixed overheads) kept EBITDA marginally above Q1 FY26 and margin at about 16.6%. Test prep (EdTech L&D) revenue fell about 15% to ₹45 crore from ₹53 crore amid MBA market churn, while DEX digital assessments revenue fell about 17% on a base effect and ₹4.7 crore of deferred revenue. Management framed Q1 as the seasonally weakest quarter and guided to Q2 and Q3 recovery for MarTech and DEX.

Management pre-bought paper ahead of expected price rises, lifting inventory and slightly raising net working capital days. Net cash reached a record Rs1,182m after Rs141m dividend, and FY27 guidance of 10-15% operating revenue growth and 17-19% EBITDA margin was reiterated.

540530|2026-06.headline: HUDCO guides FY27 disbursement of about INR65,000 crore and a INR3 lakh crore loan book by 2029-30, with spreads held near 2%.
540530|2026-06.overview: Management skipped the headline numbers and focused on policy tailwinds (urban challenge fund, bankable projects) and the pipeline. FY27 disbursement target is about INR65,000 crore against about INR5,000 crore achieved last year, with borrowing plan of about INR70,000 crore approved. Two June MoUs (Gujarat and Bihar, each above INR1 lakh crore) were presented as pipeline, with sanctions expected to start this quarter. Management reiterated a spread of around 2% and NIM of around 3%, though an analyst cited Q1 spread near 1.8%, and said compression is due to fast growth and should reverse by Q3.

financial_highlights.change: Lower due to Board decision not to create DTL on special reserve

financial_highlights.value: about INR20,000 crore; INR4,000 crore+ received in Q1

segments.name: Urban infrastructure / sustainable finance
segments.commentary: Q1 sanctions included ring roads, expressways, irrigation, water grid, industrial corridors, power generation/distribution, Telangana urban infra and water supply/sewage. Management said water and sanitation are the core sustainable-finance focus, aligned with AMRUT and MoHUA priorities.

segments.name: Housing
segments.commentary: Housing portfolio is shrinking because states are not bringing counterpart funding under PMAY; housing lending is priced around MCLR of about 8.6%.

segments.name: Private sector / PPP project finance
segments.commentary: New PPP project finance division; 2 projects sanctioned in Q1 worth about INR6,000-7,000 crore. Disbursement expected to start in the latter part of FY27. No internal target set.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement target about INR65,000 crore; borrowing plan about INR70,000 crore approved by Board.
Loan book target of INR3 lakh crore by 2030 (FY30); FY28 not planned, with mid-FY28 review and market disclosure if course correction needed.
Spread to be maintained around 2% and NIM around 3%; spread expected to reflect in Q3 as Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 disbursements capitalise.

Gujarat and Bihar MoUs (each above INR1 lakh crore; combined about INR2 lakh crore): sanctions to start in Q2 FY27 for Gujarat, with works in Q4 FY27 or earlier; MoUs valid 5 years, disbursement over around 5 years.

FX borrowing: RBI forex window tie-up of about USD2 billion (about USD700 million drawn), all-in cost about 5.5-6.5% including hedging, with ECB share possibly rising from about 10% to 20% of borrowings.
capex_capacity: Gujarat MoU: metro, RRTS, Olympic/Commonwealth Games infrastructure (Commonwealth Games Ahmedabad 2030), highways; sanctions expected this quarter.
Bihar MoU: 12 satellite towns; Bihar road projects of about INR21,000 crore identified; tourism, metro and digital parks under discussion.
Repayments of INR15,000-16,000 crore expected over remaining quarters of FY27.
demand_pricing: Analyst cited Q1 spread near 1.8%; management attributed compression to accelerated growth and expects 2% spread to return by Q3.
Competition for state financing from NABARD, NaBFID and commercial banks has pushed rates down, per management.
Borrowing mix: about 70% domestic (bank loans and bonds), about 10% ECB currently; ECB could rise to 20% over next five years.
Management said yield is not split between urban infra and housing; rates are sector-specific.

qa_highlights.question: What is the short-term foreign exposure and what are the lending rates/portfolio yield?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said short-term foreign currency loans have been retired and over 99% is 5-year borrowing. Spread guided around 2%, NIM around 3%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FX accounting loss issue behind us, and how will the Gujarat and Bihar MoUs translate into sanctions?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance director said no FCNRs maturing in FY27 or FY28 except USD200 million maturing in 2028, which is secured; no forex losses foreseen this year. Gujarat sanctions expected this quarter; Bihar has 12 satellite towns and road projects.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR3 lakh crore loan book guidance conservative given MoU visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed partly, citing land acquisition, social and political issues and state compliance before contract award; said projects typically complete within 5 years, so 5-year horizon is preferred.

qa_highlights.question: What is the internal target for private sector / PPP book?
qa_highlights.answer: No target set for private sanctions; approach is case-by-case with good entities and strong concessions. UCF PPP projects in water, desalination, drainage and sewage are expected; UCF gives 50% VGF.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 disbursement and repayment outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 disbursement about INR65,000 crore; total repayments about INR20,000 crore, with INR4,000 crore+ received in Q1 and INR15,000-16,000 crore expected in the remaining quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the forex window borrowing size and cost?
qa_highlights.answer: USD2 billion tie-up is the minimum; all-in cost including hedging about 5.5-6.5%, as RBI covers most hedging and HUDCO pays about 1.5%.

risks_watch: Spread: Q1 spread near 1.8% per analyst vs 2% guidance; watch Q2 and Q3 for recovery as higher-yield disbursements capitalise.

Tax rate change from no DTL on special reserve (effective rate about 20.6%) affects comparability.

540544|2026-03.headline: PSP Projects Q4FY26 revenue rose 66% YoY to INR1,115 crores, but a INR29 crore Kashi ECL provision kept FY26 PAT flat at INR55 crores.
540544|2026-03.overview: Q4FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR1,115 crores (up 66% YoY), with EBITDA up 85% to INR60 crores and PAT up to INR21 crores. Reported margins were depressed by a INR29 crore expected credit loss provision on unbilled revenue from the Kashi project, which took other expenses from INR17 crores to INR46 crores. For FY26, revenue grew 25% to INR3,149 crores, EBITDA rose 5% to INR189 crores with margin down to 6% from 7.14%, and PAT was flat-to-down at INR55 crores. Order book reached INR13,447 crores (up 85%) after record order inflow of INR10,925 crores, 85% of it from the Adani group.

segments.name: Adani group (in-house) orders
segments.commentary: Adani group accounted for 85% of FY26 order inflow and about INR9,000 crores (67%) of the current INR13,400 crore order book. Management says materials are pass-through on Adani contracts.

segments.name: External / non-group orders
segments.commentary: External projects are about 33-43% of the order book (about INR4,300 crores per the Q&A). Government projects fell to about 25% of the order book from 43% a year earlier.

segments.name: Precast manufacturing
segments.commentary: Current precast capacity is 3 million sq ft per year. Management says expansion to 1.5x would need only INR15-20 crores of equipment since sheds are already built. Project 90 was pre-executed in 148 days.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance is about INR4,500 crores, reiterated by management.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 7-8%, with management saying it can move 1% plus or minus; the Q&A confirmed 7-8% as the band for the next two years.
Management expects to be debt-free within about two to three quarters, with interest cost of about INR11-12 crores per quarter falling toward nil.
Working capital: trade receivable days are expected to fall to about 60 days (60-70 days per the Q&A) from about 94 days.

Order inflow is expected at INR5,000-6,000 crores from the group plus INR1,000-2,000 crores from outside in FY27. The bid pipeline is about INR6,500 crores, of which about INR5,000 crores is group and INR1,500 crores external.
Capex for FY27 is expected at about INR120-150 crores (roughly 2-4% of revenue), with quarterly lumpiness possible.
Employee cost is expected to grow about 2-4% (per the Q&A), with operating leverage as revenue rises.
Medium-term goal is 20-25% growth per year, with a target of about INR9,000-10,000 crores revenue by FY30 (per the analyst's recap, not restated by management).
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was INR192 crores; Q4FY26 capex was INR40 crores. Gross block is INR764 crores and net block INR412 crores.
Precast plant capacity is 3 million sq ft per year; management sees no major expansion needed at the current pace.
Projects under execution: 94 ongoing across Gujarat, UP, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Delhi NCR; over 256 completed to date.

Mumbai projects (Mahim, Matunga) are at early foundation stage; Matunga is at sheet piling. Tree-cutting approvals are a delay risk. Management says about INR10,000 crores of the order book is at peak execution pace.
Dharoi Dam Phase 1 was handed over and Phase 2 is in finishing. SMC RCC is complete and RVNL core and shell is complete.
demand_pricing: Order book INR13,447 crores (+85% YoY), with group projects at 67% and external at 43% per the CEO's figures (these overlap; the Q&A split is 67% Adani and 33% non-Adani).
Record FY26 order inflow of INR10,925 crores, 85% from Adani group. Major wins include SVPI Airport Ahmedabad development, Matunga Rehab Building Mumbai, and Shri Ambaji Mata Temple extension.

Key outstanding orders: Shree Ambaji Mata Temple INR966 crores, SMC Highrise INR731 crores, Human & Biological Science Gallery INR254 crores, GIFT City Fintech Building INR261 crores, Dharoi Dam INR223 crores, Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya INR216 crores, Sabarmati Riverfront Phase II INR218 crores, GIFT City residential INR210 crores.

Commonwealth Games-linked tenders (about INR7,000-8,000 crores potential, per analyst) are expected to be announced but had not been formally released; management expects them 'anytime in this quarter'.
Mobilisation advances of INR814 crores from the group are interest-free. Management says the group advance will fund most working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue guidance of INR4,500 crores and FY30 target of INR9,000-10,000 crores changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management stuck to INR4,500 crores for FY27 and said margins are improving; Q4 EBITDA margin excluding the INR30 crore provision would be about 8%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kashi ECL provision and will more come?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR29 crore provision was made because receivables beyond one year must be provided for. Management is still chasing the UP Medical College accounts through government channels and does not expect major further ECL provisions.

qa_highlights.question: How much UP Medical College money is outstanding?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR60 crores unbilled and INR40 crores trade receivable across seven projects. INR40 crores of GST invoices are pending, and final certification is awaited.

qa_highlights.question: Will PAT margin reach 4-5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to be debt-free within about two to three quarters, which would remove about INR41-45 crores of annual interest. It said PAT margin could reach 3-4% and that 4.5-5% is the target for next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook and receivable days?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days were about 90-100 at March 2026 because most revenue was booked in February and March. Management expects them to fall to around 60-70 days, with collection in April.

qa_highlights.question: Is capex/depreciation going to stay at 3% of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 capex is about INR120-150 crores, with possible flexibility to about 2% of revenue. Depreciation is expected to keep rising from new assets, so it cannot be cut.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SDB receivable status?
qa_highlights.answer: The client has just started operations. About INR90 crores of principal is in receivables, with interest billed separately. Management expects resolution during FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Adani mix or the ongoing war pressure margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most orders are Adani with pass-through materials, so it sees no major war-related margin risk. Only SMC and RVNL may see small impact.

risks_watch: Receivables jumped to INR928 crores (about 90-100 days) at March 2026; watch April-June collections against management's 60-70 day target.
Collection risk on UP Medical College (about INR60 crores unbilled and INR40 crores receivable) and the remaining Kashi and SDB balances. Further ECL provisions are possible.
Margin guidance (7-8%) depends on no further provisions. Q4 margin was depressed by the INR29 crore provision, and FY26 EBITDA margin fell to 6%.
Concentration risk: about 67% of the order book is Adani group. Mobilisation advances of INR814 crores are a funding source; a slowdown in group inflows would matter.
Execution risk in Mumbai (tree-cutting approvals, monsoon, labour availability in Q1-Q2 FY27), and the timing of Commonwealth-linked tenders.
Debt-free target and interest saving depend on collections; gross debt of about INR317 crores (INR43 crores long-term plus INR274 crores short-term) remains.

540595|2026-03.headline: Tejas Networks Q4 FY26 revenue rose 8% QoQ to INR333 crores, but Q4 PAT loss widened to INR211 crores; FY26 PAT loss INR909 crores.
540595|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR333 crores, up 8% QoQ from INR307 crores, with EBIT loss narrowing to INR219 crores from INR239 crores. PAT loss widened to INR211 crores from INR197 crores in Q3, and FY26 revenue was INR1,103 crores against a PAT loss of INR909 crores. Management described FY26 as a transition year after the BSNL 4G project, with delayed wireline and wireless projects causing a revenue shortfall, while R&D and capex were maintained. Order book closed at INR1,514 crores versus INR1,019 crores a year earlier, with India at about 88% of revenue and around 83% of order book, excluding the BSNL 4G add-on PO. Senior management and CFO changes were announced during the call.

segments.name: Wireline
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue was driven largely by wireline sales to Indian private and international customers. Shipped significant IP/MPLS routers for BharatNet Phase III, where Tejas is the largest supplier by number of circles; supplied 100G and 400G WDM systems to a Tier-1 telco.

segments.name: Wireless
segments.commentary: Signed agreement with NEC to manufacture and supply 5G Massive MIMO radios for a global customer; first PO is in the INR1,514 crores order book and revenue is expected in FY27. Received initial 4G expansion order from a South Asian customer, with some revenue booked in FY26. Multiple 4G/5G RAN field trials ongoing in South Asia and Americas; 5G POC completed in South America.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue or profit guidance given; management said it has never provided numerical guidance.
Stated goal of breakeven/PAT-positive in FY27 and PAT-positive by FY28 when asked; management said it expects better financial results in FY27 with current investments and cost structure.
Expects a good portion of the INR1,514 crore order book to convert to revenue in FY27.
Expects 5G Massive MIMO revenue from NEC contract to flow in FY27 and further 4G expansion from South Asian customer in FY27.
Expects remaining BSNL 4G collections to significantly happen in FY27, with receivables to progressively decline over the next few quarters.
R&D investment to continue but be tailored to business outlook; cost optimisation to be monitored through FY27.
Intangibles under development (up from INR400 crores to INR960 crores) expected to reach milestones over the next one to two quarters, with capitalisation on commercialisation.
capex_capacity: Intangibles under development rose from INR400 crores to INR960 crores; includes product development and technology licence/transfer from NEC; large part done, balance linked to milestones expected within one to two quarters.

Inventory of INR2,438 crores, largely procured in advance for the BSNL 4G add-on order (about 18,000 sites); inventory is usable across other 4G/4G-upgradeable-to-5G radio opportunities including private 4G networks abroad.

Product roadmap includes 1.2 Tbps per channel optical scaling to 1.6 Tbps; 5G 64TR Massive MIMO radio launched at India Mobile Congress; C+L band WDM system transmitting 76 Tbps over a single fibre pair; cloud-native converged 4G/5G core in multi-location trials; hyperscalable data center interconnect platform with over 50 Tbps in a compact footprint.
BSNL 4G/5G network went live across 100,000 sites in 2025.
Headcount approximately 2,300, broadly unchanged year on year.
demand_pricing: Order book INR1,514 crores at end Q4 FY26, about 83% India-based per analyst; excludes BSNL 4G add-on PO (about 18,000 sites), which remains under discussion with BSNL.

Management did not share deal-specific values for the NEC Massive MIMO or South Asia 4G orders; said international wireless opportunities are substantial but smaller per deal than BSNL's 100,000-site project.

Memory prices have risen; management said memory is a small share of BOM (BOM is several thousand dollars per product), and Tejas is renegotiating prices with customers and using long-term supplier contracts to protect margins.
Management said AI traffic and edge inferencing are expected to drive a network build-out cycle, with demand for 400G/800G optical and multi-terabit data centre interconnect.
Data center customers include TCS and other data center builders; a nationwide multi-terabit DWDM network for a hyperscaler in India was won.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR1,500 crore order book include the BSNL 4G project, and how much will convert to revenue this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book excludes BSNL 4G; it is from India and international wireline and wireless customers, and a good portion is expected to convert to revenue in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the NEC Massive MIMO deal in the order book, and how will it scale?
qa_highlights.answer: The first NEC PO is included in the INR1,514 crore order book; follow-on POs depend on the customer's rollout, and management expects them to be larger than the first.

qa_highlights.question: Is the BSNL 18,000-site add-on PO progressing and how fast can it be delivered?
qa_highlights.answer: Discussions are ongoing on sites and configurations; inventory is held, and delivery should be much faster as the sites are already commercial and tested.

qa_highlights.question: Are PAT-positive or breakeven targets realistic for FY27/FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not give financial guidance but that PAT-positive is the goal, with FY27 expected to show much better results and a path to profitability.

qa_highlights.question: How will receivables and inventory come down, and what if the BSNL add-on is delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: BSNL balance collections are expected significantly in FY27; receivables are shown net of BSNL advances in current liabilities. Inventory is usable across other global 4G/private network opportunities if BSNL is delayed.

qa_highlights.question: Why was intangible investment debt-funded, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said not investing in technology evolution is a bigger risk in deep-tech; FY27 investment decisions will be more tightly tied to returns and business outlook.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company expecting order wins or growth targets over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: No numerical target given; management expects growth above FY24 levels excluding one-off projects and said the investments were sized for several times FY26 revenue.

risks_watch: BSNL 18,000-site add-on PO remains unsigned; timing uncertain, with inventory build-up at risk if delayed.
Receivables of INR3,258 crores and inventory of INR2,438 crores against FY26 revenue of INR1,103 crores; collection pace from BSNL is key.
Net debt of INR3,531 crores with gross borrowings of INR4,035 crores; cash of INR505 crores.
Memory and chip cost inflation and lead-time pressure on margins; extent of price pass-through not quantified.

Leadership transition: CFO Sumit Dhingra resigning effective May 15, 2026, with AVS Prasad appointed CFO from May 16; new COO and CEO appointments subject to shareholder approval; independent director change.
Intangible assets of about INR960 crores under development, with capitalisation dependent on commercialisation.

key_quotes: So, with this trend, AI is going to drive a network infrastructure build super-cycle, which basically means that the current communication service provider networks, the CSP networks, will not be sufficient to handle the traffic growth in the coming years.
We needed a runway in FY26 to consolidate and transition our business beyond BSNL.
Yes, we've never given revenue or any other financial number guidance in the past.

But at the same time, we are positive about our future based on which we have made substantial investments during the year to make sure our products are ready, and technologically ready and capable for the business and the technology transition that we see.

540595|2026-06.headline: Tejas Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 20% QoQ to INR402 crore, with PBT still negative at INR271 crore and BSNL expansion order awaited.
540595|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR402 crore, up about 20-21% QoQ from Q4 FY26, split evenly between India and international. PBT was negative INR271 crore versus negative INR281 crore in Q4, and PAT improved slightly. Inventory eased to INR2,358 crore from INR2,438 crore, while net receivables rose to INR2,232 crore from INR1,905 crore and net borrowings reached INR4,277 crore. Management said the BSNL 26,000-site expansion order is in final stages and expected soon, and that its first international 5G end-to-end win in South America was secured.

segments.name: India (wireline and wireless)
segments.commentary: Roughly 50% of Q1 revenue, driven by domestic optical and FTTx shipments; Tier 1 telco FTTx expansion, 100G/400G DWDM for 5G backhaul and hyperscaler DC connectivity, and a large power utility modernisation win. Management does not split wireless vs wireline revenue.

540595|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations was INR406 crores in Q2 FY27 versus INR262 crores a year earlier, and H1 revenue reached INR808 crores (about 74% YoY growth). Net working capital fell to INR4,235 crores on lower receivables, while net debt rose to INR4,384 crores from INR4,277 crores as capex and operating costs were funded.

segments.commentary: Q2 revenue driven by optical IP and FTTx shipments to private operators and system integrators. Received POs for GPON FTTx from several Indian ISPs, an LOI from a new SI for IP/MPLS routers for BharatNet middle mile in 3 states, and an order for a pan-India OTN network for a Government of India enterprise.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a significant portion of the INR2,314 crore inventory to be consumed in executing the BSNL 4G order over the coming quarters.
Most of the INR1,500 crore BSNL order (LOI from TCS) is expected to convert into POs by end of Q3 FY27; only a substantial portion is in the current order book.

qa_highlights.question: How much BSNL dues have been recovered and how much is still due, and when will payment come?

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR2,300 crore order book include the INR1,500 crore BSNL order?

qa_highlights.question: Why no wins outside BSNL in India for wireless?

qa_highlights.question: Is the company partnering with GPU vendors for AI data centers, and what is the DC stage with TCS?

qa_highlights.question: What was the INR145 crore contract manufacturing loss in COGS, and will it recur?

qa_highlights.question: How much inventory and gross debt will reduce over 6 to 9 months?

540602|2026-06.headline: GTPL Hathway Q1 FY27 consolidated income rose 12% YoY to INR 1,020 crore, but net profit fell to INR 2.3 crore on higher depreciation and finance cost.

Management attributed the PAT decline of about INR 8 crore YoY mainly to a roughly INR 6 crore rise in depreciation and finance cost from capitalising right-of-use assets for HITS infrastructure. Standalone total revenue rose 16% YoY to INR 693 crore, with standalone EBITDA of INR 64.4 crore (9.3%) and net profit of INR 1.9 crore. The company signed a business transfer agreement to acquire the digital TV business of 7 ACT Group companies for INR 36.23 crore cash, with about 6 lakh subscribers, targeted to close by 15 September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ACT acquisition's expected contribution and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give revenue or EBITDA figures before closing by 15 September 2026, and said the impact would appear from Q2 and more fully in Q3, with Andhra Pradesh and Telangana leadership (over 1 million existing subs there, rising to about 1.6-1.7 million).

540602|2026-09.headline: GTPL Hathway Q2 FY27 consolidated total income rose 19% YoY to INR11,464 million, but reported EBITDA was flat at INR1,103 million (9.6% margin).

540611|2026-03.headline: AU SFB Q4 FY26 profit rose 65% YoY to ₹832 crore with ROA 1.8%, but management guided FY27 credit cost near 0.90% and flagged margin pressure.
540611|2026-03.overview: AU Small Finance Bank reported a strong Q4 FY26, with PAT up 25% QoQ and 65% YoY to ₹832 crore and quarterly ROA of 1.8%, helped by seasonal factors. Deposits grew 10% QoQ and 23% YoY, and loans grew 8% QoQ and 21% YoY, both ahead of the stated private sector benchmark of 13%. Slippages fell 17% QoQ to ₹659 crore and GNPA improved to 2.03%. Management said Q4 was flattered by seasonality, a day-count benefit and lower reversals, and that cost of funds may have bottomed after recent rate hikes.

segments.name: Retail secured (wheels, mortgages, gold)
segments.commentary: Retail secured is 66% of portfolio and grew 21% YoY. Wheels reached about ₹46,400 crore (+27% YoY), gold loans about ₹4,000 crore (doubled), and mortgages (micro business and affordable housing) about ₹42,400 crore (+11% YoY).

segments.name: Commercial banking
segments.commentary: Commercial banking is 22% of lending, at about ₹31,000 crore (+29% YoY, +12% QoQ), plus about ₹11,000 crore of non-fund book. It currently funds about 56% of its requirement internally, with a goal of full self-funding alongside transaction banking and CMS.

segments.name: Inclusive banking (MFI)
segments.commentary: Inclusive banking grew 8% QoQ. Non-overdue collection efficiency in MFI was 99.7% (vs 99.3% in Q3), and 92% of the MFI book is covered under CGFMU.

segments.name: Digital unsecured (cards and personal loans)
segments.commentary: Digital unsecured grew 4% QoQ. Personal loans rose 19% QoQ from a low base, and credit cards broadly stabilised after about five quarters of decline. Total unsecured fell 1% YoY.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Total deposits reached ₹1.52 lakh crore (+10% QoQ, +23% YoY). CASA grew 9% QoQ and 20% YoY, with CASA ratio about 28%. Branch banking is about 60% of deposits, and stable deposits are 79%.

guidance_outlook: Management guided FY27 credit cost of around 0.90% of average assets, and said Q4's 0.6% should not be used as the run-rate.
Full-year FY27 cost to assets is expected to fall below 4%, from 4.1% in FY26.

Asset mix shift toward secured assets may pressure yields, as unsecured grows slower than the rest of the book.
Management aims to grow at 2 to 2.5x nominal GDP, and said 1.8% ROA is not a permanent level. Its goal is to hold ROA around 1.8% on a full-year basis next year.
Universal bank licence: final application filed in March 2026, pending regulatory approval. Fincare core banking migration completed in April 2026.
capex_capacity: Plans to open 80 to 100 branches every year, with 2,790 touchpoints cited on the call (the 2,500 figure was corrected).
Retail secured distribution has nearly doubled in two years to about 900 to 1,000 branches per retail secured business.
First AI-native loan origination system (gold loans) went live the week before the call. Expansion to mortgages, commercial banking, wheels, personal loans and credit card LOS is underway.
Outbound AI-led calling campaigns aim to reach 25% of total calls over the next two quarters.
Organisational consolidation: agri merged into business banking, and home loans and MBL share back-end teams.
demand_pricing: Management said the home loan/affordable housing market is too competitive, with new NBFCs and HFCs entering, so it is not growing there irrationally.

Deposit rates on savings and term deposits were raised ahead of peers. Management said this reflects the mix of retail vs wholesale, CASA and CD ratio targets, and that it will be managed monthly through ALCO.
Long-term cost-of-funds aspiration is to trade near the prevailing repo rate (5.25% currently), against about 6.75% now.
Wheels growth was driven by improving affordability across segments.

qa_highlights.question: What are the details of the ₹21 crore contingency provision created in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Tripathi said these were ordinary business banking working-capital standard accounts, not high-value specific cases. The provision was added on an internal risk assessment of security cover, with no specific segment or aggregate exposure disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why were savings and term deposit rates raised well ahead of the industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Agarwal said it is a combination of how much to raise, cost of money, CASA and retail/wholesale mix and CD ratio. He noted cost of money fell 32 bps in FY26 against an expected 15-20 bps, and that liabilities are managed daily and monthly through ALCO.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable ROA and what levers drive it?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Jain said Q4 is seasonally strong and the aim is to hold ROA around 1.8% on a full-year basis next year. Levers are opex-to-assets improvement and lower credit costs from MFI and credit cards. No numeric target was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q4 margin was from IT refund and other one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Jain said the IT refund helped only slightly and was not material. He said cost of funds may have bottomed, and the seasonal benefits from lower day count and lower slippages will not recur next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How should cost-to-assets evolve as the bank moves to a universal banking licence?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Agarwal said FY27 cost to assets should go below 4%, with a first benchmark of about 3.5% in three to five years. He declined to give a number for AI-driven cost savings, calling the technology too early-stage to quantify.

qa_highlights.question: What credit cost should be assumed going forward, and how will the new RBI ECL norms affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Agarwal suggested building credit cost around 0.90%, and said Q4 should not be annualised. On ECL, management said it was too early to comment. Vivek Tripathi said 90% of the book is secured and CGFMU covers MFI, and the guideline applies from April 2027.

540611|2026-06.headline: AU SFB Q1 FY27 profit rose 37% YoY to INR796 cr, with NIM at 5.9% (+47 bps YoY) and deposits up 24% YoY.
540611|2026-06.overview: AU Small Finance Bank reported Q1 FY27 PAT of INR796 crore, up 37% YoY, driven by 41% core PPOP growth and a 47 bps YoY rise in NIM to 5.9%. Loans grew 23% YoY and deposits 24% YoY, both well ahead of private sector bank growth. Asset quality improved on a YoY basis, with slippages down 22% to INR798 crore and credit cost down 54 bps to 0.8%. Sequentially, NIM eased 7 bps and provisions rose 38% on seasonality, and an additional one-time INR23 crore provision was taken on unsecured products.

segments.name: Commercial banking

segments.name: Digital unsecured
segments.commentary: Grew 3% YoY and 7% QoQ. Personal loans +24% YoY and +19% QoQ from a low base; credit card growth marginal, with new card issuances crossing 1 lakh in Q1.

Management sees scope for improvement in opex and credit cost versus full FY26, which it says will take ROA to the guided range (target ~1.8%); CEO said the gap is about 10 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Commercial banking slippage uptick QoQ and its nature?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Tripathi said Q4 is seasonally strong, so YoY is the right comparison; commercial banking slippages are lower YoY and bank-level slippages improved about 150 bps. The QoQ uptick is in the SME book, which typically rises in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of ECL framework on steady-state credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is hard to quantify now. Models are being refined with external agencies, and Stage 3 provisions give comfort to cover incremental Stage 1 and 2 provisions. Management called the impact neutral given low LGDs; more clarity expected by end of Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Risk-adjusted yields and profitability of digital unsecured (credit cards and PL)?
qa_highlights.answer: Prince Tiwari said these are newer businesses and product-level risk-adjusted metrics are not yet meaningful. Credit cards are loss-making and PL is around breakeven, per management. Gaurav Jain said the card yield is subdued because the revolve book fell after underwriting tightening.

qa_highlights.question: NIM trajectory for the next two to three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Jain declined to give directional NIM guidance. Cost of funds has bottomed, with savings and deposit rates raised, so the cost line should be stable to slightly up depending on rates.

qa_highlights.question: MFI growth sustainability and CV credit environment?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Tripathi said the industry is recovering after degrowth and MFIN projects 17-18% growth. Q1 collection efficiency is 99.5%, and vehicle distribution has expanded in South, UP and East with no abnormal stress seen.

qa_highlights.question: Which CD ratio is used internally and NSFR range?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Agarwal said CD ratio ex-refinance is about 80% and is the internal measure. Prince Tiwari said the LCR range is about 115-120% and NSFR about 105-115%.

qa_highlights.question: ROA target of 1.8% and whether NIM is stable?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Jain said there is no NIM guidance; opex and credit cost have room to improve versus FY26. Sanjay Agarwal said the bank is about 10 bps short of the target, with other income and credit cost each contributing.

qa_highlights.question: Employee count decline and MFI credit cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Agarwal said May was the first month of manpower reduction, and back-end hiring has stopped because of AI. Front-end hiring continues for new geographies. On MFI, the 3% credit cost view is no longer the right optics; guarantee cost is now built in, so about 2.5% is possible.

CGFMU claim recovery: claims for FY26 pool expected to be lodged by end Q2 and realised around December; GNPA coverage is slightly lower than SMA coverage.

540611|2026-09.headline: AU SFB Q2 FY27 PAT up 53% YoY to INR858 Cr; deposits up 29% YoY, GNPA down to 1.99%.

Asset quality improved on a YoY basis, with GNPA at 1.99% and credit cost including guarantee premium at 0.8%, driven by unsecured normalisation. NIM fell 9 bps QoQ to 5.8% on higher investment book and seasonality, and management flagged cost-of-funds and yield pressure from the 25 bps repo hike. rows.why: 45 new deposit branches and 100+ asset centres added in Q2, 2,400 hires largely customer-facing, and deposit growth target ~25% YoY with loans at 2x-2.5x nominal GDP require continued distribution build-out, though no specific future branch count was guided.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Deposits up 29% YoY vs ~25% target, loans up 25% YoY, disbursements up 33% YoY, wheels book ~INR51,000 Cr (+27% YoY), and mortgages guided to ~20% growth next year.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management retained ~90 bps credit cost guidance and says it does not expect to reach the guided range (H1 at 73-74 bps, 81 bps incl. CGFMU), so there is no basis for raising guidance, though it is held not cut.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Drought in Central India, high oil prices and El Nino could hit asset quality in Q3, October collections are undisclosed, and the 25 bps repo hike pressures cost of funds, though management still guides ~90 bps credit cost and says Q4 shows no expected surprises.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Agentic AI LOS to extend from gold loans to wheels, mortgages and commercial loans, and Voice AI cross-lead platform covered ~5% of Q2 disbursements with ~50% opex savings on that coverage.

rows.label: Insurance fee consultation headwind to ROA
rows.why: Management acknowledged a medium-term ROA headwind of about 7-8 bps from the insurance fee consultation, partly offset by forex, credit card, trade finance and UPI MDR income.

rows.label: Cost-to-assets improvement
rows.why: Cost-to-assets ex guarantee premium at 3.9% in Q2 vs 4.0% in Q1, and management expects a YoY full-year improvement with sequential gains over multiple years.

rows.label: Southern mortgage book rebuild post Fincare
rows.why: The southern mortgage book from Fincare is being rebuilt, with mortgages growing 10-12% in core markets, and management did not give a timeline for the rebuild.

tone.note: Management was confident on deposits, growth and asset quality, and cautious on NIM and rate-cycle pass-through; analysts pushed on deposit sustainability, the 90 bps credit cost gap, and the insurance fee headwind, and management was evasive on savings/term deposit costs, CGFMU premium, and October
